Live counts are 6 sessions, 60 games, 87 winners, so nothing bites today and the projected timeline is over a year out. Low is right for a forward-looking scalability gap.

title: The backup/export tool is unreachable from the UI, exports nothing, and shows the pre-shuffled bag rather than what was actually called
summary: /admin/backup is not linked from the header nav, the admin dashboard or anywhere else — only a typed URL reaches it. What it renders is game_states.number_sequence, the full 90-ball shuffled bag generated at startGame, not called_numbers. It offers no download and omits winners, prizes, call counts and pot state, so it cannot be used to reconstruct a night.
failure_scenario: The tablet dies mid-game and the host needs the backup call sheet. Nobody can find it: NAV_ITEMS lists only Home / Sessions / Snowballs / Winners, and the admin dashboard header links only to /admin/snowball. If someone does reach /admin/backup, every game shows all 90 numbers with no marker for how far the game got, so the host cannot tell which have already been called and cannot resume. After the night, using the same page as the record of what happened is equally impossible: a game that stopped at ball 43 still lists 90, and none of the winners, prizes or the snowball settlement appear.
evidence: `grep -rn "admin/backup" src/` matches only the file's own header comment. src/components/header.tsx:8-13 NAV_ITEMS = Home, /admin, /admin/snowball, /admin/history. src/app/admin/backup/page.tsx:36 selects `game_states:game_states (number_sequence)` and :63-69 maps `game.game_states.number_sequence`. src/app/host/actions.ts:430 `const sequence = existingGameState?.number_sequence ?? generateShuffledNumberSequence();` — number_sequence is the whole pre-shuffled bag; the balls actually drawn live in the separate `called_numbers` column (supabase/migrations/20260729231945_atomic_host_mutations.sql:165 uses numbers_called_count as a cursor into number_sequence). No <a download>, no CSV/JSON generation anywhere on the page.
suggested_fix: Link the page from the header nav, scope it to one session (it currently fetches every game ever with no limit), select `called_numbers` and `numbers_called_count` alongside number_sequence so called and uncalled balls are visually separated, and add winners + prizes. If it is meant as an export, generate a CSV/JSON server-side and serve it from a route handler rather than a link the artifact sandbox or browser may block.
verify_note: All three claims check out. header.tsx:8-13 NAV_ITEMS is Home, /admin, /admin/snowball, /admin/history - no backup entry - and nothing else in src/ links the route. backup/page.tsx:36 selects game_states.number_sequence and :63-69 maps it, which is the full pre-shuffled 90-ball bag rather than called_numbers, with no cursor shown; there is no download link or CSV/JSON generation on the page, and no winners, prizes or pot state. :61 also does new Date(game.sessions?.start_date || '') which renders 'Invalid Date' on a null start_date. Severity corrected down: this is an unreachable, half-finished page that no one can currently rely on, so it degrades nothing that works today - the failure scenario is 'a tool nobody can find is also not much use'. Low, as unfinished work to either complete or delete.

title: Duplicating a session stamps the start date from UTC rather than Europe/London
summary: duplicateSession sets start_date with `new Date().toISOString().split('T')[0]`, which is the UTC calendar date. Between 23:00 and 00:00 British Summer Time that is yesterday.
failure_scenario: An admin sets up next week's session at 23:30 on Friday 14 August (BST). toISOString() yields 2026-08-14T22:30:00.000Z, so start_date is stored as 2026-08-14 rather than 2026-08-15. The admin dashboard and the backup page then show the wrong date for the copied session, and the backup page's sessions-by-start_date ordering puts it in the wrong place.
evidence: src/app/admin/actions.ts:147 `start_date: new Date().toISOString().split('T')[0],`. Live `show timezone` returns UTC, so the column default CURRENT_DATE has the same issue for createSession, which does not set start_date at all. The workspace convention requires a dateUtils helper with Europe/London; grep shows no such module in this project.
suggested_fix: Compute the date with `Intl.DateTimeFormat('en-CA', { timeZone: 'Europe/London' }).format(new Date())` (which yields YYYY-MM-DD) via a shared dateUtils helper, and consider letting the admin pick the date rather than inferring it — createSession currently gives the admin no way to set start_date at all.
verify_note: admin/actions.ts:147 is verbatim start_date: new Date().toISOString().split('T')[0], which is the UTC calendar date, and the live database timezone is UTC so the CURRENT_DATE column default has the same skew for createSession. There is no dateUtils module in this project, against the workspace convention of Europe/London formatting. The window is narrow (23:00-00:00 BST) and the consequence is a wrong date on a draft session the admin can edit before the night, plus mis-ordering on the backup page - which is itself unreachable. Low, as called.

title: Winner dates on /admin/history render in the server's UTC/en-US locale, not Europe/London
summary: HistoryPage is an async server component, so `new Date(winner.created_at).toLocaleDateString()` is evaluated in the Node process's timezone and locale — UTC and (on Vercel) en-US — rather than Europe/London. Bingo runs into the late evening, so BST wins after 23:00 local are dated to the previous day.
failure_scenario: A Full House is recorded at 00:20 on Saturday 15 August, British Summer Time. created_at stores 2026-08-14T23:20:00Z (the live database timezone is UTC). /admin/history renders '8/14/2026' — the wrong day, in US format. The admin reconciling Saturday's takings does not find the win under Saturday. The same value on /admin/sessions/[id] renders differently again, because session-detail.tsx is a client component and uses the browser's Europe/London locale, so the two admin screens disagree about the date of the same win (and the server-rendered pass of that client component produces a hydration mismatch).
evidence: src/app/admin/history/page.tsx:15 `export default async function HistoryPage()` with no 'use client' directive, and :91 `{new Date(winner.created_at).toLocaleDateString()}`. Live `show timezone` on the production database returns UTC. src/app/admin/sessions/[id]/session-detail.tsx:1 `"use client"` and :365 `{new Date(winner.created_at).toLocaleString()}` — the same data formatted in a different timezone. src/app/admin/backup/page.tsx:61 has the same server-side call, plus `new Date(game.sessions?.start_date || '')` which renders 'Invalid Date' whenever start_date is null (the column is nullable; it only defaults to CURRENT_DATE on insert).
suggested_fix: Add a dateUtils module (the workspace convention; this project has none) that formats with `Intl.DateTimeFormat('en-GB', { timeZone: 'Europe/London' })`, and use it in every admin view so server and client renders agree. Guard the backup page's start_date against null instead of passing '' to the Date constructor.
verify_note: The code facts hold: history/page.tsx:15 is an async server component with no 'use client', :91 calls toLocaleDateString() with no locale or timeZone argument, backup/page.tsx:61 does the same, and session-detail.tsx is a client component formatting the same column in the browser's locale - so the two admin screens do disagree in format. But I checked the live data and the reviewer's headline failure has never happened and is not realistic: across all 87 winners rows, zero were created at or after 22:00 UTC, and the latest created_at in the table is 2026-07-29 20:17 UTC. Bingo finishes well before the BST/UTC date boundary, so the 'wrong day' scenario does not arise. What remains is a real but cosmetic defect - dates render in the server's en-US format ('8/14/2026') instead of British ('14/08/2026'), inconsistently with the client-rendered view, against the workspace's Europe/London dateUtils convention. Low.

title: The money screen uses a browser confirm() while sessions and games use typed confirmation
summary: Deleting a snowball pot (which permanently removes its audit history and unlinks every game) and resetting one (which wipes the accumulated jackpot back to base) are both guarded by a single window.confirm, while deleting a session or a game — both of which are already blocked by the database when they matter — require typing the exact name.
failure_scenario: An admin scanning /admin/snowball clicks Reset on the wrong row and hits Enter on the browser dialog out of habit. A £300 accumulated jackpot drops to the £200 base immediately, with the only record being a history row. There is no name to type, no display of the current amount in the dialog, and no undo.
evidence: snowball-list.tsx:62 `if (confirm('Delete this snowball pot? This will unlink any games using it.'))` and :74 `if (confirm('Reset this pot to its BASE values? This clears the current jackpot.'))`. Compare src/app/admin/dashboard.tsx:119 `const isDeleteConfirmed = deleteTarget !== null && deleteTyped === deleteTarget.name;` and session-detail.tsx:270-271 for games.
suggested_fix: Use the same typed-confirmation Modal pattern for pot delete and pot reset, and put the current jackpot amount and max calls in the dialog text so the admin can see what they are about to destroy.
verify_note: The inconsistency is real and I verified both sides: snowball-list.tsx:62 and :74 are bare window.confirm strings, while dashboard.tsx:119 and session-detail.tsx:270-271 both require the exact name to be typed. The reviewer's supporting point is the strongest part of the case - sessions and games are already protected in the database by delete_session_safe and delete_game_safe, whereas nothing protects a pot reset, so the weakest confirmation sits on the only action with no backstop, and the dialog shows neither the pot name nor the amount about to be discarded. It sits close to the style-preference line the brief warns about, but a one-keystroke path from a £300 pot to base with no undo is a genuine guardrail gap rather than taste. Low.

title: The reset-session modal tells the admin it deletes snowball history that it does not touch
summary: The confirmation modal is the only place an admin learns what reset does, and one of its three bullets is false. reset_session_safe never reads or writes snowball_pot_history.
failure_scenario: An admin about to reset a session reads 'Any snowball jackpot history captured against winners in this session' will be permanently deleted, and 'Snowball pot balances and the underlying game configuration are not touched'. They reasonably conclude the pot is back to a clean slate for a replay. In fact the history claim row survives, which is exactly what makes the replay's settlement return 'already_settled' and silently strand the pot (see the reset/snowball finding). The modal actively steers the admin into the failure.
evidence: session-detail.tsx:803-810 lists 'All game states...', 'All recorded winners for this session', 'Any snowball jackpot history captured against winners in this session', then 'Snowball pot balances and the underlying game configuration are not touched.' Live reset_session_safe body touches only public.winners, public.game_states and public.sessions.
suggested_fix: Fix the behaviour first (delete the session's snowball_pot_history rows and reverse the pot inside reset_session_safe), then make the modal describe what actually happens, including naming the pot and the amount it will be moved back to.
verify_note: The copy is factually wrong. session-detail.tsx:803-810 promises 'Any snowball jackpot history captured against winners in this session' will be permanently deleted, and the live reset_session_safe body touches only public.winners, public.game_states and public.sessions - it never reads or writes snowball_pot_history. So the modal claims a deletion that does not happen, which is exactly the surviving row that strands the pot on replay. Severity corrected down: this is misleading copy on a confirmation dialog, and its harm is entirely the consequence already counted under reset-session-strands-snowball-pot. Counting it a second time at medium double-books the same failure. Low, and it should be fixed alongside that finding.

title: Unchecking every stage produces a confusing "prize required" error instead of "select at least one stage"
summary: With no stages checked, the client-side validateGamePrizes has an empty required list and passes, the submit button stays enabled, and the server then expands the empty selection back to all three default stages and fails prize validation for stages the form never rendered inputs for.
failure_scenario: An admin editing a standard game unchecks Line, Two Lines and Full House while deciding on the format. The form shows a small red 'Select at least one stage.' hint but Save Changes stays enabled. They click it. Client validation passes (requiredStages is []). On the server, `selectedStages.length > 0` is false, so stage_sequence falls back to getDefaultStagesForType('standard') = all three; the prize loop finds no `prize_Line` etc. in FormData because those inputs were not rendered, so prizes is {} and the action returns 'Game 5: prize required for Line, Two Lines, Full House' — naming stages the admin just removed. The admin cannot tell what the app wants.
evidence: session-detail.tsx:596-597 renders the hint but :715 `disabled={isSubmitting || missingPrizeStages.length > 0}` does not gate on an empty selection; :81-85 `requiredStages` returns `selectedStages` (empty) for a standard game so validateGamePrizes passes. src/app/admin/sessions/[id]/actions.ts:74-78 — `selectedStages.length > 0 ? sortStages([...selectedStages]) : getDefaultStagesForType(type)`.
suggested_fix: Disable submit when a standard game has zero stages selected, and on the server return an explicit 'Select at least one stage.' instead of silently substituting the default three.
verify_note: Traced both halves. session-detail.tsx:84-88 returns selectedStages unchanged for a standard game, so requiredStages is [] with nothing ticked and validateGamePrizes passes; :715 gates the submit button on isSubmitting || missingPrizeStages.length > 0 and never on an empty selection, so Save stays enabled despite the red hint at :597. Server-side, actions.ts:74-78 and :172-177 expand the empty selection back to getDefaultStagesForType('standard') = all three stages, and the prize loop finds no prize_ inputs for stages the form never rendered, producing an error naming the three stages the admin just unticked. Confusing but self-inflicted, non-destructive and immediately obvious to the admin. Low, as called.

title: stage_sequence is written straight from form input with no validation against the win_stage set, and can be persisted as a value no code can handle
summary: createGame and updateGame take `formData.getAll('stages') as WinStage[]` and write it into games.stage_sequence, which is plain jsonb rather than an enum array. Nothing checks the values are among 'Line' / 'Two Lines' / 'Full House'. Unlike `type` (a Postgres enum that rejects garbage) and unlike the snowball pot form (the only admin action using zod), there is no backstop.
failure_scenario: A crafted server-action POST — or a future refactor that changes the checkbox values — supplies `stages=Corners`. sortStages maps it through `stageOrder['Corners']` = undefined, giving a NaN comparator, and the row is written as `stage_sequence: ["Corners"]`. The host starts that game; record_winner_atomic derives the stage from stage_sequence[current_stage_index] and casts it to the win_stage enum, which raises, so no winner can ever be recorded on that game. The admin cannot fix it either once the game has started, because update_game_safe preserves stage_sequence for any status other than 'not_started'.
evidence: src/app/admin/sessions/[id]/actions.ts:73 `const selectedStages = formData.getAll('stages') as WinStage[]` (a bare cast, no runtime check) and :74-78 the ternary that feeds it straight into stage_sequence; same at :172-177. Live schema: `games.stage_sequence jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '["Line", "Two Lines", "Full House"]'` — jsonb, not win_stage[]. Only src/app/admin/snowball/actions.ts imports zod; grep for "from 'zod'" across src/ returns that one file.
suggested_fix: Validate every admin server action's input with zod, as the snowball actions already do: a `z.enum(['Line','Two Lines','Full House'])` array for stages, `z.enum(['standard','snowball','jackpot'])` for type, `z.coerce.number().int().min(1)` for game_index, and a `/^#([0-9a-f]{3}|[0-9a-f]{6})$/i` regex for background_colour (currently only enforced by a client-side `pattern` attribute).
verify_note: The code facts are accurate: actions.ts:73 and :172 are bare casts of formData.getAll('stages'), games.stage_sequence is jsonb rather than win_stage[], and zod is imported only in src/app/admin/snowball/actions.ts. But the severity is badly over-called because the threat model does not survive scrutiny. The only actor who can reach these actions is an authenticated admin, and the live 'Admins can manage games' policy grants that same admin blanket ALL on games - so an admin who wants a garbage stage_sequence needs no crafted server-action POST, they can PATCH the row directly. The validation therefore protects nothing against a hostile admin; it only guards against a hypothetical future refactor that changes the checkbox values, which is speculation rather than a defect. No UI path produces the failure. Low, as hardening.

title: updateSessionStatus reports success on an update it never proves landed, and permits any transition
summary: updateSessionStatus issues a bare `.update({ status }).eq('id', sessionId)` with no `.select()` — the pattern CLAUDE.md singles out as having already produced two silent-success bugs in this codebase. It also validates nothing about the transition: the caller supplies the target status and no check is made against the current one or against live games.
failure_scenario: An admin clicks 'Start Session' on a session id that no longer exists (stale tab, or the session was deleted in another window). The update matches zero rows. Supabase returns no error and no data, `if (error)` passes, and the action returns `{ success: true }`. The client calls router.refresh() and the admin believes the session is live and tells the host to start; the host dashboard shows nothing. The same shape means any RLS-filtered write would also be reported as a success. Separately, because the target status is a parameter with no state machine, a completed session can be flipped back to 'running' while its games are all 'completed', which the host dashboard will list as startable.
evidence: src/app/admin/sessions/[id]/actions.ts:309-319 — `const { error } = await supabase.from('sessions').update({ status }).eq('id', sessionId); if (error) { return { success: false, error: error.message } } ... return { success: true }`. Contrast updateSession in src/app/admin/actions.ts:89-101, which does `.select('id').single()` and treats a missing row as an error. CLAUDE.md: "Never report success on an update you have not proved landed."
suggested_fix: Add `.select('id, status').single()` and treat a missing row as an error, matching updateSession. Add an explicit allowed-transition check (draft→ready, ready→running, running→completed) and refuse to move a session out of 'running' while any of its games is in_progress.
verify_note: actions.ts:309-319 is verbatim as quoted: bare .update({ status }).eq('id', sessionId), only 'if (error)', then return { success: true }. It does violate the CLAUDE.md rule, and updateSession in admin/actions.ts:89-101 does the right thing with .select('id').single() plus a missing-row check, so the inconsistency is real. Severity over-called though. The zero-row path needs the session to have been deleted or its id to be stale, because authorizeAdmin has already proved role='admin' and the live 'Admins can manage sessions' policy is a blanket ALL, so RLS will not filter this admin's write. The second half of the claim is weaker still: 'completed' back to 'running' is the same reopen capability the Reset button exists to provide, so calling the absent state machine a defect assumes an invariant the app does not hold. A standards violation with a narrow real failure: low.

title: create_table_booking_transaction is EXECUTE-to-PUBLIC SECURITY DEFINER and belongs to no code in this project
summary: public.create_table_booking_transaction(jsonb,jsonb,jsonb) is SECURITY DEFINER owned by postgres with proacl containing `=X/postgres` (PUBLIC) and an explicit anon grant. Every other function in the schema had its anon EXECUTE revoked by the hardening migrations; this one was skipped.
failure_scenario: Anyone holding the public anon key (i.e. any punter who views /display) can POST /rest/v1/rpc/create_table_booking_transaction with attacker-chosen jsonb. It executes as the definer with RLS bypassed and performs three unconditional INSERTs into table_bookings, table_booking_items and table_booking_payments. In this database those tables do not exist so the call errors, but the grant is a permanent live-fire hazard: if that schema is ever restored, imported, or the function is re-pointed, an anonymous caller can create bookings and payment records at will. It also gives an unauthenticated attacker a definer-context error oracle.
evidence: pg_proc.proacl for create_table_booking_transaction = {=X/postgres,postgres=X/postgres,anon=X/postgres,authenticated=X/postgres,service_role=X/postgres}; prosecdef = true. Every other public function shows only {postgres,authenticated,service_role} or {postgres,service_role}. The live security advisor flags it.
suggested_fix: Drop the function if it is orphaned, which the evidence suggests (the tables it writes do not exist in this project). If it must stay, `revoke execute on function public.create_table_booking_transaction(jsonb,jsonb,jsonb) from public, anon;` in a new migration, mirroring 20260730070705.
verify_note: The grant is exactly as reported in production: proacl = {=X/postgres,postgres=X/postgres,anon=X/postgres,authenticated=X/postgres,service_role=X/postgres}, prosecdef=true, owner postgres (rolbypassrls), and it is the only public function still holding a PUBLIC/anon EXECUTE grant - every other one shows {postgres,authenticated,service_role} or {postgres,service_role}. It belongs to no code in this repo. Corrected from medium to low: I verified to_regclass returns NULL for all three of table_bookings, table_booking_items and table_booking_payments, so today the call can only raise an undefined-table error. There is no data to reach, no state to corrupt, and no money involved - it is a stale artefact worth revoking or dropping, and the residual risk is entirely hypothetical (someone later restoring that schema).

title: Two overlapping game_states INSERT policies, the narrower one dead
summary: "Hosts can insert game state" (role='host') and "Hosts/Admins can insert game state" (role in admin,host) both exist as PERMISSIVE INSERT policies. Permissive policies OR together, so the first grants nothing the second does not.
failure_scenario: No exploit today, but it is an active audit hazard: someone tightening "Hosts/Admins can insert game state" in a future migration will believe they have closed host inserts while the older policy silently keeps them open, and every INSERT pays for two profiles subqueries. The live performance advisor flags it as multiple_permissive_policies.
evidence: pg_policies returns both rows for game_states/INSERT with with_check clauses that differ only by the admin disjunct.
suggested_fix: `drop policy if exists "Hosts can insert game state" on public.game_states;` in a new migration, leaving the admin-or-host policy as the single source of truth.
verify_note: Verified live: pg_policies returns both 'Hosts can insert game state' (with_check role='host') and 'Hosts/Admins can insert game state' (with_check role in (admin,host)) as PERMISSIVE INSERT policies on game_states. Permissive policies OR together, so the narrower one grants nothing and is pure noise, and the production performance advisor flags it as multiple_permissive_policies. No exploit, correctly rated low - it is a real audit hazard for anyone later tightening the broader policy.

title: sanitizeNextUrl does not handle backslashes, so a crafted login link breaks the post-login navigation
summary: The sanitiser rejects values not starting with '/' and values starting with '//', but not '/\'. WHATWG URL parsing treats a backslash as a forward slash for http(s), so '/\\evil.com' resolves to a foreign origin.
failure_scenario: A staff member is phished with https://bingo.theanchor.pub/login?next=/%5Cevil.com. They sign in successfully, the action returns redirectTo='/\\evil.com', and router.push receives it. Next's parseRelativeUrl resolves it against the dummy base, sees a different origin and throws "invariant: invalid relative URL", so the login appears to succeed and then the page errors instead of navigating. Next's own check is what stops this becoming an actual off-site redirect; the sanitiser that exists specifically to prevent it does not catch the case.
evidence: src/app/login/actions.ts:9-14: `if (!nextUrl.startsWith('/')) return '/'; if (nextUrl.startsWith('//')) return '/';` — no backslash handling. `new URL('/\\evil.com','https://a.test')` yields https://evil.com/.
suggested_fix: Reject any next value whose second character is '/' or '\\', and drop anything containing a control character, e.g. `if (/^\/[/\\]/.test(nextUrl)) return '/'`. An allowlist of known internal prefixes ('/admin', '/host', '/') would be stronger still, since those are the only values the middleware ever sets.
verify_note: Traced: src/app/login/actions.ts:9-14 rejects only values that do not start with '/' and values starting with '//', so '/\evil.com' passes through unchanged and src/app/login/page.tsx:35 hands it to router.push. The reviewer is right that this is not an open redirect - Next's own relative-URL parsing (and the browser's same-origin rule for pushState) blocks the off-site navigation - so the worst outcome is a successful sign-in followed by a failed navigation on a phished link. Correctly rated low; the fix is one extra character class in the sanitiser.

title: Every authenticated account can read every staff email address
summary: "Authenticated users can view profiles" is `to authenticated using (true)` over a table holding id, email and role. Nothing in the app needs a user to read anyone's profile but their own (every authorizeHost / authorizeAdmin filters .eq('id', user.id)).
failure_scenario: Any host account — including one obtained through the self-signup exposure above — runs GET /rest/v1/profiles?select=email,role and gets the full staff roster with which addresses are admins. That is a ready-made target list for credential stuffing against /login, which matters more given the project has leaked-password protection disabled.
evidence: pg_policies: profiles | Authenticated users can view profiles | SELECT | roles={authenticated} | qual = true. Every call site in src/ selects role for the caller's own id only (e.g. src/app/host/actions.ts:148-151, src/app/admin/actions.ts:26-30).
suggested_fix: Narrow to `using (auth.uid() = id or exists (select 1 from public.profiles p where p.id = auth.uid() and p.role='admin'))`. Also enable leaked-password protection in the project's Auth settings, which the live security advisor reports as off.
verify_note: Verified live: 'Authenticated users can view profiles' is `to authenticated using (true)` over a table holding id, email and role, and I confirmed every call site in src/ reads only the caller's own row (`.eq('id', user.id)` at src/app/host/actions.ts:148, src/app/admin/actions.ts:27 and eight more), so `using (auth.uid() = id)` would break nothing. The current wording is a deliberate narrowing from an earlier anon-readable policy (supabase/migrations/20260430124552_tighten_profiles_select.sql), it just did not go the last step. Correctly rated low on its own - the roster is one address today - though it becomes the follow-on to the self-signup hole, since a stranger who obtains a host account can then read the full staff roster and which addresses are admin.

title: Ten native alert()/confirm() dialogs coexist with four purpose-built typed-confirm modals
summary: game-control.tsx documents replacing window.confirm with an in-app modal (line 97, "T4.3") and builds a full in-modal error system so a host behind the bar can actually read a failure. The screen immediately upstream, host/dashboard.tsx, still uses alert() three times and confirm() once, and the admin surfaces use confirm() five more times next to their own typed-confirm modals.
failure_scenario: The host taps Start on a phone. startGame fails. host/dashboard.tsx:37 fires `alert("Error starting game: " + result.error)` - a blocking OS dialog on a phone the host is holding one-handed mid-service, showing text that on the admin paths is a raw Postgres message. Worse, host/dashboard.tsx:173 gates the destructive Re-open of a finished game behind a plain confirm(), while the far less destructive delete-game on the admin screen requires typing the game name. The guardrail strength is inverted relative to the risk.
evidence: alert(): host/dashboard.tsx:37, :181, :256. confirm(): host/dashboard.tsx:173, admin/dashboard.tsx:99, session-detail.tsx:219, :231, snowball-list.tsx:62, :74. Purpose-built typed-confirm modals: session-detail.tsx:725 (delete game, types the name), :775 (reset session, types RESET), game-control.tsx:1547 (undo), :1499 (void winner, mandatory reason).
suggested_fix: Replace all ten with the existing Modal component. For host/dashboard.tsx use the inline actionError pattern already in game-control.tsx rather than alert(); for the Re-open path use a typed-confirm modal matching session-detail's delete-game modal, since re-opening a completed game is a money-adjacent action.
verify_note: Counts verified exactly: alert() at host/dashboard.tsx:37, :181, :256; confirm() at host/dashboard.tsx:173, admin/dashboard.tsx:99, session-detail.tsx:219 and :231, snowball-list.tsx:62 and :74. The inverted-guardrail point is fair: Re-open of a finished game is behind a bare confirm() at :173 while delete-game requires typing the game name. One sub-claim refuted: the alert on host/dashboard.tsx:37 shows `result.error` from startGame, and every startGame exit routes through failure()/conflictFailure() with a mapped host-facing string, so it is never raw Postgres text. A blocking OS dialog on a phone is poor, not broken.

title: authorizeAdmin is copy-pasted into three files and authorizeHost is a fourth near-copy
summary: The same 18-line authorizeAdmin function, plus its AdminAuthResult type, is duplicated verbatim in three server-action files. src/app/host/actions.ts carries a fourth copy differing only in the accepted role set.
failure_scenario: A change to the auth check (adding a suspended-account check, switching from profiles.role to a JWT claim, or wrapping auth.uid() for the auth_rls_initplan advisor) has to land in four places. Landing it in three leaves one server-action file authorising on the old rule, and because there is no test on any of them nothing catches it.
evidence: src/app/admin/actions.ts:18-37, src/app/admin/sessions/[id]/actions.ts:32-51 and src/app/admin/snowball/actions.ts:24-43 are byte-identical apart from a trailing-whitespace difference. src/app/host/actions.ts:139-158 differs only in `profile.role !== 'admin' && profile.role !== 'host'`.
suggested_fix: Create src/lib/authorize.ts exporting `authorize(supabase, roles: UserRole[])` returning the existing discriminated union, with `authorizeAdmin = (s) => authorize(s, ['admin'])` and `authorizeHost = (s) => authorize(s, ['admin','host'])`. Delete the four copies.
verify_note: Diffed the three copies: admin/actions.ts:18-37 and admin/snowball/actions.ts:24-43 are byte-identical, admin/sessions/[id]/actions.ts:32-51 differs only in trailing whitespace on one line, and host/actions.ts:139-158 is the same shape with the role test widened to admin-or-host. So the claim is exactly right. Downgrading severity: this helper is defence in depth, not the gate. Every write these actions perform is additionally constrained by RLS keyed on profiles.role (sessions/games/snowball_pots are all admin-ALL policies) or routed through a SECURITY DEFINER RPC that calls assert_is_admin(). A copy left behind would produce a wrong error message, not an unauthorised write.

title: next.config.ts is empty: no typed routes, no bundle analysis, and browserslist data is eight months stale
summary: next.config.ts contains only a `/* config options here */` comment. There is no typedRoutes, no bundle analyzer, no image config. postcss.config.mjs runs autoprefixer on top of @tailwindcss/postcss, which already prefixes via Lightning CSS. caniuse-lite is eight months old, so autoprefixer's targets are wrong.
failure_scenario: The pub TV is the oldest browser this app has to serve, and it is the one surface where prefixing and target data matter (globals.css:232 keeps a -webkit-mask-image prefix by hand "for older TV browsers"). With eight-month-stale caniuse data, autoprefixer's decisions about that TV's browser are guesses. Separately, without typedRoutes, a typo in one of the ~20 hand-written route strings (`/host/${sessionId}/${nextGameId}` in revalidatePath, `router.push(result.redirectTo)`) is a runtime 404 rather than a compile error, and revalidatePath silently revalidates nothing when the path is wrong.
evidence: next.config.ts:3 `const nextConfig: NextConfig = { /* config options here */ };`. `npx browserslist` prints "Browserslist: browsers data (caniuse-lite) is 8 months old. Please run: npx update-browserslist-db@latest". postcss.config.mjs lists both "@tailwindcss/postcss" and "autoprefixer". package.json has no typecheck script despite CLAUDE.md documenting `npm run typecheck`.
suggested_fix: Set `typedRoutes: true` in next.config.ts and fix whatever it surfaces. Run `npx update-browselist-db@latest` and commit the lockfile change. Drop autoprefixer from postcss.config.mjs and from devDependencies. Add `"typecheck": "tsc --noEmit"` to package.json so the documented command exists.
verify_note: All three facts reproduce: next.config.ts is an empty object with the scaffold comment, postcss.config.mjs runs autoprefixer alongside @tailwindcss/postcss, and `npx browserslist` prints the eight-month caniuse-lite warning. Severity is over-called. An empty next.config.ts is the Next default and typedRoutes is opt-in, so calling its absence a defect is a preference; stale caniuse data changes which prefixes autoprefixer emits, and the one hand-written prefix the finding cites (globals.css:232) is hand-written precisely so it does not depend on autoprefixer. No user-visible consequence was demonstrated.

title: Four user-facing dates are formatted with raw Date methods and no timezone, against the workspace date rule
summary: There is no dateUtils module in this project. Four display sites call toLocaleString()/toLocaleDateString() with no locale and no timeZone, and one write site derives a date from a UTC ISO string.
failure_scenario: admin/backup/page.tsx:61 and admin/history/page.tsx:91 are server components, so toLocaleDateString() runs on the Vercel server in UTC with the server's default locale, giving American M/D/YYYY ordering to a British pub. session-detail.tsx:365 is a client component so it renders in the viewer's locale, meaning the same winner timestamp reads differently on two admin screens. duplicateSession (admin/actions.ts:147) sets start_date from `new Date().toISOString().split('T')[0]`, which during British Summer Time between 00:00 and 01:00 local yields yesterday's date.
evidence: session-detail.tsx:365 `{new Date(winner.created_at).toLocaleString()}`; admin/history/page.tsx:91 `{new Date(winner.created_at).toLocaleDateString()}`; admin/backup/page.tsx:61 `(new Date(game.sessions?.start_date || '')).toLocaleDateString()`; display/page.tsx:50 the same; admin/actions.ts:147 `start_date: new Date().toISOString().split('T')[0]`. No src/lib/dateUtils.ts exists.
suggested_fix: Add src/lib/date-utils.ts with `formatDateInLondon` and `formatDateTimeInLondon` (Intl.DateTimeFormat with locale 'en-GB' and timeZone 'Europe/London') plus `getTodayIsoDate()` for the duplicateSession write, and route all five sites through it.
verify_note: All five sites verified and there is no src/lib/dateUtils.ts in this project. admin/backup/page.tsx:61, admin/history/page.tsx:91 and display/page.tsx:50 are server components, so toLocaleDateString() resolves against the Vercel runtime's locale and UTC rather than Europe/London, while session-detail.tsx:365 is a client component resolving against the viewer - so the same winner timestamp can genuinely read differently on two admin screens. duplicateSession (admin/actions.ts:147) does derive start_date from a UTC ISO string, which lands a day early between 00:00 and 01:00 during BST. Correctly scored low: admin-facing display ordering and one duplicated session's default date, all correctable in the UI.

title: Dead exported server actions, dead component variants, no-op CSS classes and leftover authoring comments
summary: A cluster of dead surface and leftover scaffolding: two exported server actions with no callers, unused component variants, four uses of an undefined CSS class, and thinking-out-loud comments left in shipped UI primitives.
failure_scenario: Each item is individually harmless but collectively they make the codebase read as unfinished and mislead the next reader. `signup()` and `voidWinner()` are 'use server' exports, which means Next publishes a POST endpoint for each; both are unreachable from any UI. session-detail.tsx:575, :599, :627 and :676 apply `text-muted-foreground`, a shadcn token defined nowhere in this project, so the class resolves to nothing (it happens to be paired with text-yellow-200/80, so the text is still visible - it is dead, not broken). BingoBall's `normal` and `mini` variants and the getBallColor path that serves them are never used; only `active` and `called` are.
evidence: `grep -rn '\bsignup\b' src/` returns only the definition at login/actions.ts:40. `grep -rn 'voidWinner\b' src/` returns the definition at admin/sessions/[id]/actions.ts:357 and a comment reference in host/actions.ts:1337. button.tsx:4-9 contains "We need to install class-variance-authority for this pattern, or just write it manually. For now, I'll write it manually to avoid extra deps if possible… Let's stick to simple props for now". bingo-ball.tsx:35 "Only color the active ball for now, or maybe all white balls?" and :36 "Let's style the text color for normal balls too". `grep -rn 'text-muted-foreground|border-destructive' src/` returns 5 hits, and neither token is defined in tailwind.config.ts or globals.css (only `.text-destructive` is, at globals.css:222). `variant="normal"` and `variant="mini"` have no call sites.
suggested_fix: Delete signup() (the login UI has no sign-up affordance and the comment's 'stable hook' argument does not justify a live endpoint), and either wire voidWinner into the admin winners table or delete it in favour of voidWinnerFromHost. Delete the `normal` and `mini` BingoBall variants. Replace text-muted-foreground with a defined class and drop the redundant border-destructive. Remove the authoring commentary from button.tsx and bingo-ball.tsx.
verify_note: Every item checks out. `signup` appears only at its definition (login/actions.ts:40); `voidWinner` (admin/sessions/[id]/actions.ts:357) has no caller, only a comment reference from host/actions.ts:1337 - and it is the copy that implements the .select() rule correctly, so the good pattern is the dead one. text-muted-foreground appears at session-detail.tsx:575, :599, :627, :676 and border-destructive at :661, and neither token is defined in tailwind.config.ts or globals.css. BingoBall's 'normal' and 'mini' variants have no call sites (only 'active' and 'called' are used, at game-control.tsx:1096/:1241 and player-ui.tsx:854), and the authoring comments are at bingo-ball.tsx:35-36 as quoted. Tidy-up, correctly scored low; both dead server actions are behind authorizeAdmin so the published endpoints are not an exposure.

title: Two pairs of near-identical host server actions, one pair already drifted on a guard
summary: moveToNextGameOnBreak (841-911) and moveToNextGameAfterWin (913-979) are 66 lines each and differ only by a trailing toggleBreak call. advanceToNextStage (1151-1226) and skipStage (1410-1486) are the same read-state / read-game / compute-index / conditional-update / settle-pot flow, and have already drifted apart.
failure_scenario: skipStage guards `if (totalStages === 0) return failure('This game has no stages set up.')` (line 1440). advanceToNextStage has no such guard: with an empty stage_sequence it computes newStageIndex = 0+1 = 1, sees 1 >= 0, sets newStageIndex = -1 and newGameStatus = 'completed', and writes current_stage_index = -1 to game_states. The public surfaces then read `stage_sequence[-1]` and render undefined for the stage name. The same defect fixed once in skipStage is still open in advanceToNextStage, which is exactly what duplicated flows produce.
suggested_fix: Extract `advanceStage(supabase, controlResult, gameId, { clearWinDisplay: boolean })` covering the shared body and have both actions call it, so the totalStages guard and the pot-settlement path exist once. Extract `moveToNextGame(currentGameId, sessionId, cashJackpotAmountInput, { startOnBreak: boolean })` for the other pair. Drop the unused select columns at line 1172.
verify_note: The duplication is real: moveToNextGameOnBreak (841-911) and moveToNextGameAfterWin (913-979) differ only by the trailing toggleBreak, advanceToNextStage (1151-1226) and skipStage (1410-1486) are the same flow, and advanceToNextStage:1172 does select `type` and `snowball_pot_id` without reading them. The failure is refuted. advanceToNextStage can only write current_stage_index = -1 if stage_sequence is empty, and it cannot be: createGame (admin/sessions/[id]/actions.ts:74-79) and updateGame (:173-178) both build stage_sequence server-side as ['Full House'] for snowball/jackpot, or sortStages(selectedStages) when the form supplied any, or getDefaultStagesForType(type) which returns ['Line','Two Lines','Full House'] otherwise. There is no path producing []. skipStage's totalStages === 0 check at :1440 is defensive, not a fix for a bug that is still open in the twin.

title: The host dashboard's Start / Resume / Re-open button has no in-flight guard
summary: game-control.tsx carries nine separate per-action in-flight flags with a comment explaining why ("A publican taps twice on a phone, so every mutation gets its own flag and its own disabled control", line 110). The Start/Resume/Re-open button on host/dashboard.tsx has no such flag and is never disabled while startGame is in flight.
failure_scenario: A host on pub wifi taps Start, sees nothing happen for two seconds, and taps again. Two startGame calls run concurrently. The server-side conditional updates bind status, so the second returns a conflict rather than corrupting state, but that conflict surfaces as `alert("Error starting game: The game changed while you were acting. Refreshed now.")` on a game that in fact started correctly. The host now believes the start failed.
evidence: host/dashboard.tsx:164-186 renders the Button with no `disabled` prop and an onClick that awaits startSelectedGame with no re-entrancy check. The only in-flight state in the file, isSubmittingCashJackpot, guards the modal path (line 271) but not the direct path. Compare game-control.tsx:112-120, nine flags.
suggested_fix: Add `const [startingGameId, setStartingGameId] = useState<string | null>(null)` and gate both the handler and `disabled={startingGameId !== null}`, matching the pattern in game-control.tsx.
verify_note: Read host/dashboard.tsx:164-186: the Start/Resume/Re-open Button has no disabled prop and its onClick awaits startSelectedGame with no re-entrancy check, while the only in-flight flag in the file (isSubmittingCashJackpot) guards the modal path only. The consequence is exactly as described and no worse: startGame's branches all bind the status they read (`.eq('status','not_started')` at :462, `.eq('status','in_progress')` at :443, `.eq('status','completed')` at :425, plus the unique-violation catch at :477), so the second tap returns a conflict rather than wiping a board - it just tells the host the start failed when it succeeded. Contrast game-control.tsx's nine per-action flags. Low is right.

title: Closing a stacked modal restores body scrolling while the modal underneath is still open
summary: Modal's effect sets document.body.style.overflow = 'hidden' when open and, in its cleanup, sets it to 'unset' unconditionally. Modals in this app stack: Record Winner opens on top of the Claim Check modal, and Post Win opens on top of both.
failure_scenario: The host has the Claim Check modal open (game-control.tsx:1279, a full-height modal with a scrollable 90-number grid). Check Win succeeds and opens Record Winner on top (line 1596). The host taps Cancel. Record Winner's cleanup runs `document.body.style.overflow = 'unset'` while the Claim Check modal is still open, so the page behind now scrolls under the host's thumb while they re-count a ticket on a phone. The same happens every time Post Win is closed.
suggested_fix: Replace the direct style write with a module-level open-modal counter: increment on open, decrement on close, and only restore overflow when the count reaches zero. Also record and restore the previous overflow value rather than hard-coding 'unset'.
verify_note: Traced both halves. src/components/ui/modal.tsx:78-85 sets body overflow 'hidden' on open and unconditionally 'unset' in cleanup keyed on [isOpen], and because the component stays mounted with isOpen false, closing the upper modal re-runs that cleanup. The stacking is real: handleOpenRecordWinnerModal (game-control.tsx:891-898) sets showWinnerModal true without touching showValidationModal, which is only cleared later at :873 after a successful record, and isActionErrorShownInModal at :1033 ORs all six modal flags precisely because they coexist. So cancelling Record Winner restores scrolling under an open Claim Check modal. Real, reproducible, and annoying on a phone mid-claim, but nothing is lost or mispaid.

title: Eleven raw console.error/warn calls bypass the redaction helpers, one logging two UUIDs
summary: The project has two deliberate logging helpers: logError (dev-only, redacts UUIDs) and logActionFailure (always logs, redacts UUIDs, drops Postgres details/hint so prize amounts do not reach the logs). Eleven call sites use console.error/console.warn directly instead, including three inside server code that runs in production.
failure_scenario: src/app/host/[sessionId]/[gameId]/page.tsx:67 emits `console.warn(\`Game ${gameId} in session ${sessionId} has no initial game state...\`)` on every host navigation to a game with no state row. Both UUIDs land unredacted in the Vercel production logs, which is precisely what the UUID_RE in log-action-failure.ts and log-error.ts exists to prevent. admin/snowball/actions.ts:126 and :253 log raw Supabase error messages from the money audit path with no redaction.
evidence: grep of console. across src/ excluding the two log helpers returns 11 hits: host/page.tsx:39, host/dashboard.tsx:180, host/[sessionId]/[gameId]/page.tsx:47,:59,:67, admin/sessions/[id]/page.tsx:62,:84, admin/snowball/actions.ts:126,:253, admin/history/page.tsx:46, admin/backup/page.tsx:44. log-action-failure.ts:13 `const UUID_RE = /[0-9a-f]{8}-.../gi` with the comment "Never pass a user id, a session name or a prize value to either function."
suggested_fix: Replace every console.error/warn in src/app with logError (server components) or logActionFailure (server actions), and pass identifiers as separate structured fields the helper can redact rather than interpolating them into the message string. Add an ESLint no-console rule with an override for src/lib/log-*.ts.
verify_note: Reproduced the grep: exactly 11 console.* calls outside the two helpers, at the lines listed, including host/[sessionId]/[gameId]/page.tsx:67 emitting both gameId and sessionId unredacted from a server component. Correcting severity down. The stated harm is a privacy one and does not apply: a game id and a session id are opaque UUIDs for a pub's own fixtures, not player-identifying data, and CLAUDE.md's anonymity rule is about winner names. The other two production-path sites (snowball/actions.ts:126, :253) log `auditError.message`, which log-action-failure.ts's own SAFE_ERROR_FIELDS classifies as safe. This is a consistency and log-hygiene point.

title: resetSnowballPot reads the same pot row twice for data it already holds
summary: resetSnowballPot fetches the pot selecting base_max_calls, base_jackpot_amount, current_max_calls and current_jackpot_amount into `oldPot`, then immediately fetches the same row again selecting base_max_calls and base_jackpot_amount into `pot`, and uses `pot` for the update while `oldPot` supplies the audit values.
failure_scenario: Beyond the wasted round trip, the two reads are not in the same transaction, so if the pot's base values change between them the update writes one snapshot while the audit row records another - an audit trail that does not match the write it is describing.
suggested_fix: Delete the second query and use oldPot.base_max_calls / oldPot.base_jackpot_amount in the update. Better, fold the read, the update and the audit insert into one security-definer function as the settle path already does.
verify_note: Verified at admin/snowball/actions.ts:208-227: oldPot already selects base_max_calls and base_jackpot_amount alongside the current values, and the second read into `pot` fetches the same two columns from the same row for no reason. The second query is entirely redundant, which is a cleaner statement of the defect than the audit-mismatch angle - the mismatch needs another admin to edit the pot's base values in the window between two consecutive reads, which is vanishingly narrow. Low is right.

title: Three overlapping colour systems, with a 200-line !important override sheet that leaks the old pink brand on admin focus rings
summary: The Anchor rebrand was implemented as ~200 lines of `.anchor-theme .<old-class> { ... !important }` overrides repainting the previous pink/indigo/slate theme, applied by LayoutContent only on non-game pages. Alongside it, tailwind.config.ts still defines the old bingo.* palette (pink/amber/indigo, still referenced 21 times) and components carry 390 raw hex literals. Which system a class belongs to determines whether it renders green or pink, and the answer depends on the route.
failure_scenario: globals.css:146 overrides `.anchor-theme .ring-bingo-primary` but there is no override for the variant selectors `.focus-visible\:ring-bingo-primary:focus-visible` or `.focus\:ring-bingo-primary:focus`. Every form control on /admin therefore shows a pink #EC4899 focus ring on the green Anchor page: the game type select (session-detail.tsx:568), the stage checkboxes (:591), the notes textarea (:709), and the same three controls on admin/dashboard.tsx:241 and :251. Same gap for `group-hover:text-bingo-primary` on display/page.tsx:49. More broadly, a new admin component written with `bg-slate-800` silently renders green while one written with `#0f6846` renders green too, and the same `bg-slate-800` on a host page renders slate, so the correct way to write a colour depends on which route the component will be mounted under.
evidence: grep of globals.css finds only `.anchor-theme .ring-bingo-primary` at line 146, no focus/focus-visible variant. Usage counts across src/: 21 bingo-* class references, 63 bg-slate-* references, 390 six-digit hex literals in src/app + src/components, 4 uses of the declared --anchor-* CSS variables. layout-content.tsx:22 applies anchor-theme only when `!isGamePage`.
suggested_fix: Pick one system. Define the Anchor palette once as tokens (either in tailwind.config.ts under `theme.extend.colors.anchor` or as @theme in globals.css), rewrite the slate/indigo/bingo class usages in src/app/admin/** and src/app/display/page.tsx to those tokens, then delete the .anchor-theme override block and the bingo.* palette. Until that lands, add the missing focus-visible and group-hover overrides so the pink stops showing.
verify_note: Verified. globals.css:2 carries `@config "../../tailwind.config.ts"`, so the v3-style bingo.* palette (primary #EC4899 pink) does generate under Tailwind v4. globals.css:146 defines only `.anchor-theme .ring-bingo-primary`, and grep shows no bare `ring-bingo-primary` anywhere in src - every usage is the variant form (`focus-visible:ring-bingo-primary` at admin/dashboard.tsx:241, session-detail.tsx:568 and :709; `focus:ring-bingo-primary` at admin/dashboard.tsx:251, session-detail.tsx:591), which compiles to `.focus-visible\:ring-bingo-primary:focus-visible` and is not matched by that override. So the override is dead code and the focus rings are pink on the green admin pages. Correcting severity: the entire observable consequence is the colour of a focus ring on an admin-only screen. That is cosmetic. The three-overlapping-systems point is a fair maintainability note but does not lift it to medium.

title: Two incompatible server-action error conventions: host actions redact and map, admin actions return raw Postgres messages
summary: src/app/host/actions.ts has a full error discipline: failure()/conflictFailure()/rpcFailure()/relayFailure(), a HOST_RPC_ERRORS map turning raised keys into plain host-facing words, a conflict flag and a machine-readable code, with raw messages routed to logActionFailure which strips UUIDs and drops Postgres `details`/`hint` so prize amounts never land in logs. The three admin action files use none of it and return `{ success: false, error: error.message }` in fifteen places, with no logging at all.
failure_scenario: An admin tries to delete a session with a foreign-key dependency. The browser renders the raw Postgres text, for example 'insert or update on table "games" violates foreign key constraint "games_snowball_pot_id_fkey"' plus a DETAIL clause. Per the log-action-failure.ts comment, Postgres puts the failing row into DETAIL on constraint violations, so a winners-related failure would put prize_description (a cash amount) on screen. Nothing is logged server-side, so the failure is also undiagnosable after the fact.
evidence: src/app/admin/actions.ts lines 64, 97, 119, 159, 186; src/app/admin/sessions/[id]/actions.ts lines 120, 142, 152, 230, 279, 297, 316, 336, 350, 379; src/app/admin/snowball/actions.ts lines 69, 103, 112, 147, 161, 171, 180, 215, 239 all return `error.message` verbatim with no logActionFailure call. Contrast src/app/host/actions.ts:79-86: `function failure(action, hostMessage, logged = hostMessage) { logActionFailure(action, logged); return { success: false, error: hostMessage } }`.
suggested_fix: Move failure/conflictFailure/rpcFailure/relayFailure and the ActionFailure type from src/app/host/actions.ts into src/lib/action-result.ts and use them from all four action files. Give each admin failure a plain-English host message and pass the Supabase error object as the `logged` argument.
verify_note: The pattern is real: 12 sites (not the 15 claimed, and several cited line numbers are wrong) return `error.message` verbatim with no logging - admin/actions.ts:64,97,119; admin/sessions/[id]/actions.ts:120,230,297,315,379; admin/snowball/actions.ts:69,112,180,239 - against host/actions.ts's failure()/conflictFailure()/rpcFailure()/relayFailure() discipline at :79-86 with HOST_RPC_ERRORS at :44-68. The leak scenario is refuted. src/lib/log-action-failure.ts:23 defines SAFE_ERROR_FIELDS = ['message','code'] and drops details/hint precisely because Postgres puts the failing row in DETAIL, so the project's own helper classifies `message` as safe to surface. PostgREST returns the row values in error.details, not error.message, so no prize_description reaches the admin's screen. What is left is raw Postgres wording on an admin-only screen and no server-side log line.

title: Small typing weaknesses: a boolean|null control flag, a silent role downgrade, and a missing exported return type
summary: The codebase is otherwise strongly typed with no `any`, no `as any` and no ts-ignore anywhere. Three residual weaknesses stand out.
failure_scenario: (1) canTakeControl is `!controlling_host_id || (controller_last_seen_at && ...)`, whose type is boolean|null rather than boolean; when a controller is set but controller_last_seen_at is null it evaluates to null, which is falsy, so the Take Control button is hidden. The server-side takeControl explicitly treats a null heartbeat as "not a live lock" (host/actions.ts:534-535, `'controller_last_seen_at.is.null'`), so the client hides a button the server would honour, and a host locked out by a null-heartbeat controller has no way in. (2) page.tsx:117 `currentUserRole={profile?.role || 'host'}` silently downgrades an admin to host when the profiles read fails, removing the Void Winner control that is the documented only escape from an undo blocked by a winner on the last ball. (3) `cn()` has no explicit return type, against the workspace rule for exported functions.
evidence:
game-control.tsx:149-150:
    const canTakeControl = !currentGameState.controlling_host_id ||
        (currentGameState.controller_last_seen_at && (new Date().getTime() - new Date(currentGameState.controller_last_seen_at).getTime() > 30000));
host/actions.ts:544-549 `.or(['controlling_host_id.is.null', ..., 'controller_last_seen_at.is.null', ...])`. host/[sessionId]/[gameId]/page.tsx:117. src/lib/utils.ts:6 `export function cn(...inputs: ClassValue[]) {`.
suggested_fix: Rewrite canTakeControl as an explicit boolean that mirrors takeControl's four conditions, including the null-heartbeat case, and pull the 30000 literal from a shared CONTROLLER_HEARTBEAT_TIMEOUT_MS constant rather than duplicating the magic number the server already names (host/actions.ts:19). Make the role prop required and fail the page render if the profile read fails, rather than defaulting. Add `: string` to cn.
verify_note: Mixed, and the headline item is refuted. (1) canTakeControl at game-control.tsx:149-150 is indeed boolean|null, but the state it misbehaves on is unreachable: every write to controlling_host_id also writes controller_last_seen_at in the same object (host/actions.ts:391, :416, :449, :537), so a live controller with a null heartbeat does not occur, and takeControl's `controller_last_seen_at.is.null` clause at :547 is belt-and-braces rather than a case the client contradicts. (2) is real and the reason I am not refuting outright: host/[sessionId]/[gameId]/page.tsx:32-36 ignores the profiles read error and :117 then does `profile?.role || 'host'`, so a transient read failure silently downgrades an admin and hides the Void Winner control that is the documented only way out of an undo blocked by a winner on the last ball - no security consequence, since voidWinnerFromHost re-checks role server-side at host/actions.ts:1352, and a reload clears it. (3) cn() lacking a return type is a style rule. Low overall.

title: The two money helper modules, jackpot.ts and snowball.ts, have no tests at all
summary: Eleven of the fifteen src/lib modules have a co-located .test.ts. The four without are jackpot.ts, snowball.ts, log-action-failure.ts and utils.ts (whose tests live oddly at tests/utils.test.ts instead of beside the source). jackpot.ts and snowball.ts both decide money.
failure_scenario: parseCashJackpotAmount strips every non-digit and non-dot character before parsing: `Number(input.replace(/[^0-9.]/g, ''))`. A host typing '2,50' for two pounds fifty gets 250, and formatCashJackpotPrize writes '£250 Cash Jackpot' into games.prizes for every stage, which is what the display, the player phone and the winners row all show. A host typing '£12.50 (cash)' gets Number('12.50') = 12.5, correct by luck. There is no test asserting either case. Separately, isSnowballJackpotEligible (`numbersCalledCount <= maxCalls`) is the client-side gate that decides whether the host is even shown the Eligible / Not eligible choice; its boundary at exactly maxCalls is untested on the client side even though the same boundary is re-checked in SQL.
evidence: `for f in src/lib/*.ts; do [ -f "src/lib/$(basename $f .ts).test.ts" ] || echo $f; done` -> jackpot.ts, log-action-failure.ts, snowball.ts, utils.ts. jackpot.ts:22 `const numeric = Number(normalized.replace(/[^0-9.]/g, ''));`. snowball.ts:17-19 `isSnowballJackpotEligible(n, max) { return n <= max }`.
suggested_fix: Add src/lib/jackpot.test.ts covering parseCashJackpotAmount with '250', '£250', '2,50', '1,000', '12.50', '0', '-5', '' and '1.2.3', plus isCashJackpotGame's three branches. Add src/lib/snowball.test.ts covering getSnowballWindowStatus and isSnowballJackpotEligible at n = max-1, max and max+1, and formatPounds with 100, 100.5, 100.50 and NaN. Add src/lib/log-action-failure.test.ts asserting UUIDs are redacted and that `details`/`hint` are dropped. Move tests/utils.test.ts to src/lib/utils.test.ts.
verify_note: Verified: src/lib has co-located tests for 11 modules and none for jackpot.ts, snowball.ts, log-action-failure.ts or utils.ts (whose tests sit at tests/utils.test.ts). jackpot.ts:22 is `Number(normalized.replace(/[^0-9.]/g, ''))` as quoted. The failure scenario is weak for this app: in British input a comma is the thousands separator, so '£1,000' -> 1000 is correct and is the case the strip exists for; '2,50' is a continental decimal comma that a Sussex publican is not going to type. isSnowballJackpotEligible is a one-line `<=` whose binding copy is re-derived inside record_winner_atomic anyway, so the client boundary being untested cannot pay a jackpot wrongly. A genuine coverage gap on two money helpers, but no demonstrated defect.

title: Five .update() calls report success without proving the write landed, against the codebase's own documented rule
summary: CLAUDE.md states every direct .update() must .select() and treat zero rows as an error, and two files in this repo carry comments explaining why (host/actions.ts:1377, admin/sessions/[id]/actions.ts:369). Five other .update() calls still check only `error` and never look at rows.
failure_scenario: Concrete on resetSnowballPot: an admin opens /admin/snowball, another admin deletes a pot, the first admin clicks Reset. The update at snowball/actions.ts:229 matches zero rows, PostgREST returns no error and no rows, so `if (error)` passes. The action then inserts a snowball_pot_history row at line 243 recording old_val_jackpot -> new_val_jackpot for a change that never happened, and returns success. The money audit trail now contains a fabricated entry. Second case: api/setup/route.ts:91 updates profiles.role='admin' for a user whose profiles row was never created; zero rows, no error, and the endpoint responds {success:true, role:'admin'} while the user has no admin access at all.
evidence: admin/sessions/[id]/actions.ts:309-312 `.from('sessions').update({ status }).eq('id', sessionId)` then `if (error)`. admin/snowball/actions.ts:106-113 and 229-240, same shape. host/actions.ts:298-302 `.from('sessions').update({status:'completed', active_game_id:null}).eq('id', sessionId)` with the result discarded entirely. api/setup/route.ts:91-98. Compare host/actions.ts:1381-1397, which does it correctly and explains why.
suggested_fix: Append `.select('id')` to each and treat an empty array as a failure, matching voidWinnerFromHost. For resetSnowballPot in particular, move the pot update and the audit insert into a single security-definer function the way settle_snowball_pot already does, so the audit row cannot outlive a failed update.
verify_note: All five sites verified as described (admin/sessions/[id]/actions.ts:309, admin/snowball/actions.ts:106 and :229, host/actions.ts:298, api/setup/route.ts:91), and they do violate the rule CLAUDE.md states and that voidWinner at admin/sessions/[id]/actions.ts:369-382 follows correctly. Both concrete failures are refuted. resetSnowballPot: the described race cannot land, because two preceding `.single()` reads of the same pot (lines 208 and 219) return PGRST116 and bail if another admin deleted it, and RLS cannot filter the update since 'Admins can update pots' is an ALL policy and the caller is already authorizeAdmin-verified; only a deletion inside the window between the second read and the update produces a fabricated audit row. api/setup: I queried production - auth.users has an on_auth_user_created trigger running handle_new_user(), and 1 user / 1 profile / 0 missing, so a user with no profiles row is not a real state, and the route uses the service-role client which bypasses RLS anyway. Real pattern debt, no demonstrated wrong outcome.

title: The display has no audio of any kind, though PRD 3.1 lists Win / Break / Start sound effects as in scope for v1
summary: docs/PRD.md section 3.1 In scope (v1) ends with "Sound effects for the display client (Win, Break, Start)". There is no Audio, no <audio>, no .mp3 and no sound asset anywhere in the project. CLAUDE.md's "no audio" note is specifically about number announcements, which is a different thing.
failure_scenario: A Full House lands during the loudest part of a Friday night. The pub TV flips to a silent WIN! overlay. Half the room, facing the bar rather than the screen, misses the transition entirely and keeps marking, so the host has to shout over the room to stop play - which is exactly the moment a late claim becomes possible and the house rule "claims must be called on the number they're won on" becomes contentious.
evidence: `grep -rni "audio|\.mp3|sound" src` returns nothing. `ls public` returns only the two logo PNGs. docs/PRD.md 3.1: "**Sound effects** for the display client (Win, Break, Start)." CLAUDE.md's exclusion is narrower: "It does not broadcast number announcements with audio (no react-player)."
suggested_fix: Add three short bundled sounds triggered off display_win_type transitions, on_break transitions and game start, behind a mute toggle persisted on the display device (the TV laptop is set up once). If sound is genuinely unwanted, delete the line from the PRD so it stops reading as an open requirement.

title: The ticket colour is spelled out in words only on the host briefing; the pub TV and the follower phone paint the colour and never name it
summary: getColourName was written specifically so a colour is communicated as a word rather than a hue, and its own comment names accessibility as the reason. It is imported in exactly one place: the host's pre-game briefing. Both public surfaces render background_colour as a wash with no accompanying colour name.
failure_scenario: A colour-blind punter (roughly 1 in 12 men, and this is a pub) looks at the TV to work out which page of the book is in play for Game 4. The screen is washed in a colour they cannot name and nothing on it says "Peach". They have to ask a neighbour, or mark the wrong page and only discover it when their claim is refused - which, under the house rule shown on that same screen, cannot be re-claimed later.
evidence: `grep -rn "getColourName" src` returns src/lib/colour-name.ts (definition + test) and src/components/host/pre-game-briefing.tsx:22 only. src/lib/colour-name.ts:26-28: "The host is colour-blind; the colour word is the accessibility primary." display-ui.tsx and player-ui.tsx both read `background_colour` for styling and never call getColourName.
suggested_fix: Render `{getColourName(game.background_colour)} book` next to the game name on both /display and /player. It is a one-line change per surface and reuses the tested helper.

title: The unindexed-FK, auth_rls_initplan and multiple_permissive_policies advisor warnings are noise at this data volume
summary: I checked each performance advisor item against real table sizes. The whole database is under 1 MB and the largest table is 87 rows, so none of the nine unindexed foreign keys or the per-row `auth.uid()` re-evaluations can matter. The one item worth a tidy is the genuinely duplicated INSERT policy on game_states, which is redundant rather than slow.
failure_scenario: No failure. Documenting so these are not treated as outstanding work: the sequential scans the advisor is warning about are over 60- and 87-row tables. `winners.game_id` is the only unindexed FK on a live-game code path (`void_last_number` and `settle_snowball_pot` both scan `winners` by `game_id` while holding a row lock) and at 87 rows that scan is sub-millisecond. Revisit if `winners` ever passes a few thousand rows.
evidence: Live sizes from pg_stat_user_tables / pg_total_relation_size: winners 87 rows / 80 kB, game_states 60 / 344 kB, game_states_public 60 / 152 kB, games 60 / 88 kB, sessions 6 / 64 kB, profiles 1 / 32 kB, snowball_pots 1 / 32 kB, snowball_pot_history 0 / 48 kB. The duplicate policies are real: `game_states` has both "Hosts can insert game state" (from 20251221101436:11, host only) and "Hosts/Admins can insert game state" (from 20251221101438:13, admin or host); the second strictly contains the first. Repo and production agree on both, so this is not drift.
suggested_fix: Drop the redundant "Hosts can insert game state" policy on `game_states` in a one-line migration. Leave the FK indexes and the `auth.uid()` wrapping alone until table volumes justify them; if you want the advisor quiet, wrap the policy calls as `(select auth.uid())`, which is behaviour-preserving.
verify_note: Independently verified: winners 87 rows, games 60, sessions 6, whole database 16 MB, so the unindexed-FK and auth_rls_initplan advisories cannot matter at this scale. The duplicate permissive INSERT policies on game_states are real and confirmed in pg_policies - "Hosts can insert game state" (host only) and "Hosts/Admins can insert game state" (admin or host), the second strictly containing the first - and repo and production agree, so it is redundancy not drift. This entry claims no failure and is a correct triage note rather than a defect; low is right and no action is required beyond optionally dropping the redundant policy.

title: create_table_booking_transaction exists in production but no migration creates it, so it would vanish on a rebuild
summary: This is the only object in the live `public` schema that no repo migration creates. Three migrations discuss it and deliberately leave it alone, but none defines it, so a project rebuilt from `supabase/migrations/` would not have it. It is also the one function still holding PUBLIC and anon EXECUTE.
failure_scenario: If the project is ever rebuilt from migrations (fresh project, branch database, the `supabase/tests/run.sh` harness), this function is absent. Whatever calls it — the migration comments guess "likely used by public booking form", and it is not this app — breaks with no warning. Conversely, in the live database it is a SECURITY DEFINER function callable by anon that inserts into `table_bookings`, `table_booking_items` and `table_booking_payments`, none of which exist in this project, so every call fails with `relation does not exist`. Whichever way round it is, the repo and production disagree about whether this object should exist.
evidence: Live `pg_proc` for schema public lists 15 functions; 13 are defined by repo migrations, `handle_new_user` comes from the baseline, and `create_table_booking_transaction` comes from nowhere. Its ACL is `=X/postgres | postgres=X/postgres | anon=X/postgres | authenticated=X/postgres | service_role=X/postgres` — PUBLIC plus anon, unlike every other function. Its body inserts into `table_bookings` / `table_booking_items` / `table_booking_payments` and casts to `table_booking_type` / `table_booking_status`, none of which exist in this database (`list_tables public` returns 8 tables, none of them). `grep -rn create_table_booking_transaction .` finds only comments in three migrations, no definition.
suggested_fix: Decide and record it: either drop the function from production (it cannot succeed here — its target tables do not exist) or add a migration that creates it so the repo is a complete description of the database. Either way, revoke the PUBLIC and anon EXECUTE while it remains.
verify_note: Verified: pg_proc for schema public lists 15 functions including create_table_booking_transaction (prosecdef=true, owner postgres) whose proacl is `{=X/postgres, postgres=X, anon=X, authenticated=X, service_role=X}` - the only function still holding both PUBLIC and anon EXECUTE. grep across the repo finds it only in comments in three migrations, never a CREATE FUNCTION, so a rebuild from supabase/migrations/ would not produce it and the repo/prod histories disagree about whether it should exist. It is also inert here: it writes to table_bookings / table_booking_items / table_booking_payments, none of which exist in this database. Low is right - it belongs to another product, so the action is to decide and document, not to change behaviour.

title: display_winner_name is rendered on both public screens but every write path sets it to null
summary: `game_states.display_winner_name` exists on both tables, is selected by the display and player queries, and both UIs render a prominent heading when it is truthy — but every code path that writes it writes `null`, including `record_winner_atomic`. It is dead weight that reads like a live feature.
failure_scenario: No runtime failure; the block simply never renders. The cost is that the column looks like a supported feature to the next person, and it sits directly against the documented policy that winners are anonymous and no player-identifying data is stored. Someone wiring it up to a real name would satisfy the type system and the schema while breaking that policy.
evidence:
Every occurrence in src/app/host/actions.ts (lines 415, 448, 678, 709, 742, 788, 1126, 1194, 1461) is `display_winner_name: null`. Prod `record_winner_atomic` sets `display_winner_name = null` in its final update. Reads: `{currentGameState.display_winner_name && (

{currentGameState.display_winner_name}

)}` in display-ui.tsx:1030 and the equivalent in player-ui.tsx:750. CLAUDE.md: "`winners.winner_name` is always 'Anonymous'. There is no UI input for a winner name and no plan to add one."
suggested_fix: Drop the render blocks and the column from the SELECT lists, and add a comment on the column recording that it is retained only for schema stability — or drop the column from both tables in a migration once the reads are gone.
verify_note: Verified: all nine occurrences in src/app/host/actions.ts write `display_winner_name: null`, the prod atomic-host-mutations migration sets `display_winner_name = null` in both its win-display updates, and the only reads are the conditional headings at display-ui.tsx:1030 and player-ui.tsx:750, which can therefore never render. Dead code that reads as a live feature, sitting against the documented anonymous-winners policy. The reviewer states no runtime failure, and there is none. Low is right; the honest fix is to drop the reads or the column, not to wire it up.

title: The schema has no CHECK constraints at all, so every invariant depends on application code holding
summary: `pg_constraint` for schema public contains only primary keys, uniques and foreign keys — zero CHECK constraints. Money can go negative, call counts can go out of 1..90, `called_numbers` can drift from `numbers_called_count`, and `winners.session_id` need not agree with `games.session_id`. All of these are currently enforced only inside the RPCs, which several RLS policies let callers bypass.
failure_scenario: Concrete reachable case: a host inserts a `winners` row directly (see the winners-INSERT finding) with `session_id` set to a different session from the game's. `record_winner_atomic` would have raised `wrong_session`, but the direct insert has no such check and no FK spans both columns. The win then appears under the wrong session on /admin/history and in the `delete_session_safe` winner count, so the right session becomes deletable and the wrong one does not. Second case: `updateSnowballPot` accepts `current_jackpot_amount` from a zod schema with `min(0)` but nothing stops a direct `PATCH /rest/v1/snowball_pots` by an admin writing a negative jackpot, which then propagates into the display copy shown to punters. Third case: `game_states.numbers_called_count` is nullable with no range check, so a bad direct write can put the ball counter above 90 or below 0 and `call_next_number`'s `v_count >= jsonb_array_length(number_sequence)` guard reads a nonsense cursor.
evidence: `select conrelid::regclass, conname, contype from pg_constraint where connamespace='public'::regnamespace` returns 22 rows, all contype p, u or f — no contype 'c'. Nullable-with-default columns that the code always coalesces: game_states.numbers_called_count, current_stage_index, status, call_delay_seconds, on_break, paused_for_validation, called_numbers; winners.prize_given, is_snowball_jackpot, is_void. Live data is currently clean: bad_seq_len 0, dup_seq 0, count_mismatch 0, bad_count 0, bad_win_count 0, stage_not_in_seq 0.
suggested_fix: Add the cheap ones in one migration: `check (numbers_called_count between 0 and 90)` and `check (current_stage_index >= 0)` on game_states; `check (current_jackpot_amount >= 0 and base_jackpot_amount >= 0 and current_max_calls between 1 and 90 and base_max_calls between 1 and 90)` on snowball_pots; `check (call_count_at_win is null or call_count_at_win between 1 and 90)` on winners. For the session/game agreement, either drop the direct-insert path (preferred, see the winners-INSERT finding) or add a composite FK `winners(game_id, session_id) references games(id, session_id)` backed by a unique index on `games(id, session_id)`.
verify_note: The factual core holds: `select count(*) from pg_constraint where connamespace='public'::regnamespace and contype='c'` returns 0, and the nullable-with-default columns are as listed. Severity medium->low: every failure scenario offered needs a hand-crafted PostgREST call by authenticated staff. Case one is the winners-INSERT finding restated (already scored there, double counting it here inflates the picture). Case two is an admin PATCHing a negative jackpot, which is the owner-role attacking their own data. Case three needs a direct write to game_states by a host or admin. Live data is clean on every invariant I checked (0 null numbers_called_count/status/called_numbers, 0 null is_void/is_snowball_jackpot/prize_given, 0 winners whose session_id disagrees with their game's session_id). Adding CHECKs is sound defence in depth, not a live integrity failure.

title: The profiles INSERT policy checks only the id, so it would grant self-promotion to admin if a profile row were ever absent
summary: "Users can insert their own profile." has `with check (auth.uid() = id)` and says nothing about `role`. It is currently unexploitable only because `handle_new_user` creates a row for every auth user and there is no DELETE policy on `profiles`, so the primary key always blocks the insert.
