failure_scenario: Any change that removes a profile row without removing the auth user — a manual dashboard tidy-up, a future admin "deactivate user" feature, or a data restore that misses `profiles` — leaves that user able to `POST /rest/v1/profiles` with `{id: <their own uid>, role: 'admin'}`. The policy passes and they are an admin, gaining `snowball_pots` write access and the `winners` UPDATE that CLAUDE.md defends at length. It is one deleted row away from privilege escalation.
evidence: Live policy: profiles | "Users can insert their own profile." | INSERT | with_check `(auth.uid() = id)`. Live policies on profiles are INSERT, SELECT (authenticated), UPDATE (admin) — no DELETE policy today. `profiles_id_fkey FOREIGN KEY (id) REFERENCES auth.users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE`. Live data: 1 profile, role admin.
suggested_fix: Tighten the WITH CHECK to `auth.uid() = id and role = 'host'::public.user_role`, or drop the policy entirely — `handle_new_user` is SECURITY DEFINER owned by postgres on a table without FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY, so it does not need any INSERT policy to work.
verify_note: Policy verified live: profiles INSERT "Users can insert their own profile." with_check (auth.uid() = id), no constraint on role, and profiles has INSERT/SELECT/UPDATE policies only. Currently unexploitable as the reviewer says: handle_new_user creates the row for every auth user and there is no DELETE policy, so the primary key blocks the insert. I also checked the obvious bypass - a PostgREST upsert (Prefer: resolution=merge-duplicates) takes the ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE path, which Postgres requires an UPDATE policy for, and that one is admin-only, so it is blocked too. Latent one-deleted-row-away escalation, worth adding `and role = 'host'` or similar to the WITH CHECK. Low is right.

title: The two admin snowball pot writes use .update() with no .select(), the exact pattern CLAUDE.md forbids, on the money table
summary: `updateSnowballPot` and `resetSnowballPot` call `.update(...).eq('id', id)` and check only `error`. A Supabase update that matches no row — stale id, or RLS filtering — returns no error and no rows, so the action reports success while the pot is unchanged. CLAUDE.md names this exact failure mode and says it had already bitten the snowball pot once.
failure_scenario: The admin has /admin/snowball open in a tab while the pot is deleted or its id changes in another session. They submit an edit: the prior `.select()` of the old values fails and the action bails, so today the id-not-found case is caught by luck rather than design. The uncaught case is an RLS change or a role downgrade between the `authorizeAdmin()` check and the update (the check reads `profiles.role`, the update re-evaluates the policy independently): the update matches zero rows, `error` is null, the action returns `{ success: true }`, the admin sees the pot page reload with the old figures and reasonably assumes a caching glitch. On a jackpot table, a false success is money reported wrong.
evidence: `const { error } = await supabase.from('snowball_pots').update(parsed.data).eq('id', id); if (error) { return { success: false, error: error.message } }` (updateSnowballPot, line 107) and the same shape at line 230 in resetSnowballPot. Contrast `voidWinner` in src/app/admin/sessions/[id]/actions.ts:369, which adds `.select('id')` and treats zero rows as an error, with a comment explaining why. CLAUDE.md: "Every direct `.update()` must either `.select()` and treat zero rows as an error, or go through an RPC that returns the persisted value."
suggested_fix: Add `.select('id, current_max_calls, current_jackpot_amount')` to both updates and return a failure when zero rows come back, or fold both into the RPC suggested for the audit-trail finding.
verify_note: Code shape verified: updateSnowballPot line 105-111 and resetSnowballPot line 228-238 both do .update(...).eq('id', id) and inspect only `error`, with no .select() and no RPC returning the persisted value, which is exactly what CLAUDE.md forbids on this table. Severity medium->low: the reviewer's own analysis concedes the stale-id case is already caught by the preceding .select().single() fetch that bails on a missing pot, so the only surviving path is an RLS or role change landing between authorizeAdmin() and the update within the same request, i.e. a millisecond-wide race that cannot realistically fire on a bingo night. Worth fixing as a one-line hardening to match voidWinner (src/app/admin/sessions/[id]/actions.ts:369), but no reachable wrong-money outcome exists today.

title: Two comments still cite migration filename 20260730120000, which no longer exists after the July reconciliation
summary: The 2026-07-30 filename reconciliation renamed `20260730120000_atomic_snowball_settlement.sql` to `20260730065531_...` and the winner-idempotency migration to `20260730064309_...`, but two references were missed, including one baked into a live column comment in production.
failure_scenario: Someone auditing which migration introduced `winners.client_request_id` follows the comment to `20260730120000`, finds no such file, and cannot tell whether the migration was lost or renamed. This matters more than usual here because the repo's own MEMORY note records that repo and production histories were reconciled 1:1 and must stay that way.
evidence: src/types/database.ts:346 `// on every row written before 20260730120000. Not player-identifying.` and docs/architecture/overview.md:94 `20260730120000_atomic_snowball_settlement.sql`. The live column comment on `winners.client_request_id` carries the same stale version: "Null on every row written before 20260730120000...". Actual files: `supabase/migrations/20260730064309_winner_idempotency_key.sql` and `supabase/migrations/20260730065531_atomic_snowball_settlement.sql`, both matching `supabase_migrations.schema_migrations`.
suggested_fix: Update both comments to the real filenames. The live column comment can be corrected in the same migration as any other change, or simply left — but note in `docs/architecture/data-model.md` that the production comment carries the pre-reconciliation version.
verify_note: Verified: src/types/database.ts:346 and docs/architecture/overview.md:94 both cite 20260730120000, and the actual files are 20260730064309_winner_idempotency_key.sql and 20260730065531_atomic_snowball_settlement.sql. I found a third reference the finding does not mention, in supabase/migrations/20260730064309_winner_idempotency_key.sql:64, which is the COMMENT ON COLUMN text that also propagated the stale version into the live winners.client_request_id comment (that one is inside an applied migration and should be corrected by a new comment migration, not by editing history). Documentation accuracy only, no behaviour affected. Low is right.

title: src/types/database.ts is hand-maintained and claims a dozen live-nullable columns are non-null
summary: The file is hand-written (it carries prose comments a generator would not produce) and its Row types mark many columns non-null that are nullable in production. It is internally inconsistent about it: `winners.is_void` is correctly `boolean | null` with a long comment about why, while `winners.is_snowball_jackpot` — nullable in exactly the same way and read by the same money logic — is typed `boolean`.
failure_scenario: A developer writes a jackpot report and, trusting `is_snowball_jackpot: boolean`, filters with `.eq('is_snowball_jackpot', false)` to list non-jackpot wins. Postgres drops NULL rows from an `= false` comparison, so any pre-default or hand-inserted row silently disappears from the report. This is precisely the trap the neighbouring `is_void` comment warns about, and TypeScript gives no hint because the type says the column can never be null. Same shape for `game_states.numbers_called_count`, `status`, `called_numbers` and `sessions.status`: strict-mode TS will not force a null check on a value the database can return as null.
evidence: Live `information_schema.columns` is_nullable = YES for: sessions.start_date, sessions.status, sessions.is_test_session; games.type, games.background_colour, games.prizes; game_states.called_numbers, numbers_called_count, current_stage_index, status, call_delay_seconds, on_break, paused_for_validation, updated_at (and the same set on game_states_public); winners.prize_given, is_snowball_jackpot, is_void; profiles.role, profiles.created_at; snowball_pot_history.created_at. In src/types/database.ts all of these except `is_void` are typed non-null. The file also declares `Enums: { [_ in never]: never }` while the live schema has five enums (user_role, session_status, game_status, game_type, win_stage).
suggested_fix: Regenerate with `supabase gen types typescript` into a `database.generated.ts`, keep the hand-written prose in a thin wrapper that re-exports it, and reconcile the differences. If regeneration is not wanted, at minimum change `is_snowball_jackpot` to `boolean | null` and carry the same comment as `is_void`.
verify_note: Verified: src/types/database.ts is hand-written (prose comments throughout), types winners.is_snowball_jackpot as `boolean` while is_void is honestly `boolean | null` with a comment warning about this exact trap, and types game_states.numbers_called_count / status / called_numbers and sessions.status non-null despite information_schema reporting them nullable; the Enums block is `{ [_ in never]: never }` while five enums exist live. Severity medium->low: no current code filters those columns with .eq(), and production contains zero nulls in every one of them (defaults populate on insert), so there is no runtime failure today and TypeScript types do not affect behaviour. It is a real trap for the next developer and a regeneration/annotation job, not a defect in the running system.

title: game_states.updated_at is frozen at insert time and mirrored into the public table, where four queries still select it
summary: `updated_at` has `default now()` but there is no BEFORE UPDATE trigger to maintain it and none of the RPCs or server actions ever set it, so it records when the row was created, not when it last changed. The sync trigger faithfully copies the stale value into `game_states_public`, and four query strings still request it.
failure_scenario: Anyone reaching for `updated_at` to answer "is this screen stale?" or "which snapshot is newer?" gets a timestamp that has not moved since the game state row was first written. Live proof: game d681eec1 has `updated_at = 2026-07-29 18:23:11` while `last_call_at = 2026-07-29 18:38:36` and `state_version = 190` — fifteen minutes and 190 updates later. CLAUDE.md warns "Don't trust `updated_at` for ordering. Use `state_version`", which understates it: the column is not merely unreliable, it never changes at all.
evidence: Live triggers on game_states: only `bump_game_state_version` (BEFORE UPDATE, sets state_version) and the two `sync_game_states_public` triggers. `grep -rn "updated_at" src` outside src/types/database.ts returns only the four SELECT column lists (display/page.tsx:21, display-ui.tsx:103, player/page.tsx:20, player-ui.tsx:95) — no assignment anywhere. Live row sample confirms the freeze.
suggested_fix: Either set `new.updated_at := now()` inside the existing `bump_game_state_version` BEFORE UPDATE trigger (one line, no new trigger), or drop the column from the four SELECT lists and from `game_states_public` so nobody can be misled by it.
verify_note: Verified exactly. Live triggers on game_states are only bump_game_state_version (BEFORE UPDATE, body sets nothing but state_version) and the two sync_game_states_public triggers; no BEFORE UPDATE touches updated_at and grep finds no assignment anywhere in src. Live proof reproduced: game d681eec1 has updated_at 2026-07-29 18:23:11 against last_call_at 18:38:36 and state_version 190, and two further rows show the same freeze. The column is selected in four query strings but never used in any comparison, so nothing currently misbehaves; the risk is a future reader trusting it. Low is right.

title: The Manual Snowball Win button stays enabled on a completed or paused game
summary: Every other host control is gated by `isGameCompleted` / `isGameNotInProgress` / `isPausedForValidation`. The Manual Snowball Win button is gated only by `!isController` (via a `pointer-events-none` wrapper) and by the presence of a pot.
failure_scenario: Host presses browser Back from the new game to the finished snowball game, or is still on the page after the game completed. The amber "🏆 Manual Snowball Win" button is live. Tapping it mints a fresh claim key, sets a prize description of `£<jackpot> (Manual Snowball Win)` and opens the award modal, which reads as a live jackpot payout. `record_winner_atomic` refuses with `not_in_progress` so no money moves - the server is sound - but the host has been walked all the way to a Confirm button on the one action in the app that pays out the jackpot, on a game that is over. Recovery: none needed, but it is the wrong affordance to leave live.
evidence: `{game.type === 'snowball' && currentSnowballPot && (<div className={cn("flex justify-center mb-8", !isController && "opacity-50 pointer-events-none")}><Button ... onClick={() => { ... manualSnowballRequestIdRef.current = newClaimRequestId(); setShowManualSnowballModal(true); }}>🏆 Manual Snowball Win</Button>` - no `disabled` prop at all. Contrast `isNextNumberDisabled`, `isBreakToggleDisabled`, `isValidateButtonDisabled`, `isVoidLastNumberDisabled`, which all include `isGameCompleted`.
suggested_fix: Add `disabled={!isController || isRecordingSnowballWinner || isGameNotInProgress || isGameCompleted}` to match the rest of the pad.
verify_note: Confirmed at game-control.tsx:1216-1234: the button has no `disabled` prop, gated only by `game.type === 'snowball' && currentSnowballPot` and a `!isController && 'opacity-50 pointer-events-none'` wrapper, in contrast to isNextNumberDisabled/isBreakToggleDisabled/isValidateButtonDisabled/isVoidLastNumberDisabled which all fold in isGameCompleted. The live record_winner_atomic body confirms `if coalesce(v_state.status,'not_started') <> 'in_progress' then raise exception 'not_in_progress'`, so no money can move and the reviewer says so. Wrong affordance on the one control that pays the jackpot, no functional consequence: low is correct.

title: A game completed via `skipStage` or `advanceToNextStage` leaves `ended_at` null and the session pointing at a finished game
summary: `endGame` sets `ended_at`, clears `sessions.active_game_id` and normalises the session status. The two other paths that can set `status='completed'` - `advanceToNextStage` past the last stage and `skipStage` on the last stage - do neither: they write the status, settle the pot, call `maybeCompleteSession` and stop.
failure_scenario: Host validates a Full House claim on the last game, then taps "Skip (No Winner)" rather than recording it. `skipStage` sets `status='completed'` with `ended_at` still null and settles the snowball pot, but `sessions.active_game_id` still points at the now-finished game and the session is not tidied unless every game happens to be complete. The host is left on a completed game page with no Post Win modal and no next step, and `/admin/history` has a completed game with no end time. The pub TV falls back to the waiting screen (because `hasRenderableGame` requires `status === 'in_progress'`), so guests see nothing wrong, but the session record is inconsistent and, if the host closes the tab here, the session stays `running`.
evidence: `skipStage` update object: `{ current_stage_index: newStageIndex, status: newStatus, paused_for_validation: false, display_win_type: null, display_win_text: null, display_winner_name: null }` - no `ended_at`. Same in `advanceToNextStage`. `endGame`'s update by contrast is `{ status: 'completed', ended_at: new Date().toISOString(), on_break: false, ... }` and is followed by the `active_game_id` clear-down block.
suggested_fix: Have both paths route their completion through `endGame` (or share its tail), so `ended_at`, the pot settlement, `maybeCompleteSession` and the `active_game_id` clear-down always happen together whichever control finished the game.
verify_note: Verified both update objects. skipStage (actions.ts:1452-1465) and advanceToNextStage (1188-1196) write status 'completed' with no ended_at and no active_game_id clear-down, while endGame (781-788) writes ended_at and follows with the session tidy-up. So a game completed via either stage path leaves ended_at null in /admin/history and sessions.active_game_id pointing at a finished game unless maybeCompleteSession happens to complete the whole session. The 'no next step' part is softer than stated - the host can go back to /host and start the next game from the dashboard - and guests see the normal waiting screen. Record inconsistency and a missing end time: low.

title: The session-completion writes are never proved to have landed, against the codebase's own documented rule
summary: `maybeCompleteSession` fires `.update({ status: 'completed', active_game_id: null })` with no `.select()`, no zero-row check and not even an error check - the result is discarded entirely. `endGame`'s follow-up "clear the active game" write checks `error` but likewise has no `.select()`. CLAUDE.md states the rule explicitly: a Supabase `.update()` that RLS filters out returns no error and no rows, so `if (error)` passes while nothing is written.
failure_scenario: The final game of the night ends. `maybeCompleteSession` runs, its update is filtered or fails, and nothing anywhere notices - there is no `if (error)`, no log line, no host-facing message. `endGame` then re-reads the session, sees it is not `completed`, and writes `{ active_game_id: null, status: 'running' }` instead. The session is left running for ever, which is the same end state as the abandoned-game case: next week's `/display` shows a picker instead of the game, and if the last game was the snowball game the audit trail is misleading. The host is told the game ended successfully. This is the one path where a silent write failure produces exactly the symptom that is hardest to attribute, because it surfaces a week later on a different screen.
evidence: `if (!hasIncompleteGame) { await supabase.from('sessions').update({ status: 'completed', active_game_id: null }).eq('id', sessionId) }` - the awaited result is not assigned or inspected. And in `endGame`: `const { error: clearActiveError } = await supabase.from('sessions').update(clearActiveGameUpdate).eq('id', sessionId); if (clearActiveError) { ... }` with no `.select()`. Compare `voidWinnerFromHost` in the same file, which does `.select('id')` and treats zero rows as an error, with a comment explaining exactly why.
suggested_fix: Add `.select('id')` to both writes and treat zero rows as a logged failure; at minimum, log the error from `maybeCompleteSession` rather than discarding it. The session-completion write is the one place where a silent no-op is invisible until the following week.
verify_note: The code claim is accurate: maybeCompleteSession (actions.ts:296-302) awaits `.update({status:'completed', active_game_id:null}).eq('id', sessionId)` and discards the result entirely - no error check, no log, no .select(); endGame's clear-active write (actions.ts:825-833) checks error but has no .select(). That is a straight deviation from the CLAUDE.md rule. But the stated failure mechanism is refuted: the write cannot be RLS-filtered here. authorizeHost (actions.ts:152) only admits role 'admin' or 'host', and live policy list gives 'Admins can manage sessions' (ALL) and 'Hosts can update sessions' (UPDATE), so both callers pass. The only realistic trigger is a transient DB error, and on the endGame path the follow-up re-read partly self-heals by clearing active_game_id. Missing proof on a write that in practice lands - worth fixing for the rule, but not a medium-probability failure.

title: Manual Snowball Win is offered at any stage and on a completed game, and fails with a misleading refusal
summary: The button is gated only on `game.type === 'snowball' && currentSnowballPot`, but the action it fires always claims stage 'Full House', so on any earlier stage the server raises `stage_mismatch` and the host is told the live stage has moved on.
failure_scenario: Host is on the Line stage of a snowball game and taps Manual Snowball Win to pre-award a jackpot. `record_winner_atomic` computes `v_expected_stage = 'Line'`, raises `stage_mismatch`, and the host sees "The live stage has moved on. Refreshing now." — which is untrue and gives no hint that the button only works during Full House. On a completed game the same tap yields "This game is not in progress."
evidence:
game-control.tsx:1217 `{game.type === 'snowball' && currentSnowballPot && ( ... )}` — no stage or status condition.
game-control.tsx:1884 `'Full House', // Assume Snowball is always FH`
Live `record_winner_atomic`: `v_expected_stage := v_game.stage_sequence ->> coalesce(v_state.current_stage_index, 0); if v_expected_stage is null or v_expected_stage <> p_stage::text then raise exception 'stage_mismatch'; end if;`
HOST_RPC_ERRORS maps `stage_mismatch` to 'The live stage has moved on. Refreshing now.' (actions.ts:49).
suggested_fix: Only render the button when `currentStageName === 'Full House'` and the game is in progress, or disable it with a tooltip explaining it is a Full House control.
verify_note: Verified: the button's only condition is `game.type === 'snowball' && currentSnowballPot` (1217) - no stage, no status - and the handler hard-codes 'Full House' (1884). Live record_winner_atomic raises stage_mismatch when v_expected_stage <> p_stage, and actions.ts:49 maps that to 'The live stage has moved on. Refreshing now.', which is untrue on an earlier stage and gives no hint the button is Full-House-only. Safe (the server refuses) and cosmetic in consequence, so low.

title: `maybeCompleteSession` swallows read errors and updates `sessions` without `.select()`, so a session can silently stay 'running' forever
summary: The helper that closes a session returns silently on any read error and finishes with a bare `.update()` whose row count is never checked, which is precisely the failure shape CLAUDE.md warns about; callers treat its completion as success.
failure_scenario: Host ends the last game of the night. The `game_states` read inside `maybeCompleteSession` returns a transient error, so the function returns without doing anything. `endGame` then reads the session, sees status still 'running', and sets `active_game_id = null, status = 'running'`, returning success. The host is navigated to `/host` and the session still appears under RUNNING with every game showing "Re-open". `/display` still resolves the session as active. Nothing tells anyone the session was never closed, and an admin has to fix it by hand.
evidence:
actions.ts:283 `if (error || !games || games.length === 0) return;`
actions.ts:292 `if (completedStatesError) return;`
actions.ts:298-302:
```
await supabase
    .from('sessions')
    .update({ status: 'completed', active_game_id: null })
    .eq('id', sessionId)
```
No `.select()`, no row-count check, no return value. Callers ignore it entirely: actions.ts:813 `await maybeCompleteSession(supabase, sessionId);`, and the same at 1222 and 1482.
CLAUDE.md gotcha: "Every direct `.update()` must either `.select()` and treat zero rows as an error, or go through an RPC that returns the persisted value."
suggested_fix: Return a result from `maybeCompleteSession`, add `.select('id')` to the update and treat zero rows as a failure, log the swallowed read errors via `logActionFailure`, and have `endGame` surface "the game ended but the session did not close" the way it already does for the `active_game_id` clear at line 832.
verify_note: The code reads as described (actions.ts:283, 292, 298-302 - two silent returns and a bare .update() with no .select()), but the reviewer's framing over-states it on two counts. The CLAUDE.md gotcha it invokes is about RLS-filtered updates being reported as success; live policies make that leg inapplicable here - sessions has 'Admins can manage sessions' ALL and 'Hosts can update sessions' UPDATE using role='host', so neither caller is filtered out. What is left is the real defect: a transient read error returns silently and the session is simply not auto-completed, leaving it RUNNING with active_game_id null. That is recoverable from /admin and breaks nothing live. Missing guardrail, not a user-visible live-game failure.

title: After "Close and stay paused" the main control pad has no Resume control, contradicting the modal's own instruction
summary: While `paused_for_validation` is true, Next Number, Take Break and Undo Last Call are all disabled and no Resume button is rendered on the page, so the only route out of the pause is to reopen the claim-check modal and press "Cancel & Resume".
failure_scenario: Host records a winner, then taps "Close and stay paused" to hand out the prize. The Post Win modal closes and the page shows "CHECKING CLAIM...". The host wants to carry on: NEXT NUMBER is disabled, Take Break is disabled, Undo Last Call is disabled. The modal's own copy told them to "Resume ... from the main pad", but the only enabled control that leads anywhere is "Check Claim", which re-pauses and then has to be cancelled. Mid-game, behind the bar, this reads as a frozen app.
evidence:
game-control.tsx:1779-1781 `"Closes this box and leaves the game paused with the win on screen. Resume or check another claim from the main pad when you are ready."`
game-control.tsx:1022 `const isNextNumberDisabled = ... || isPausedForValidation || ...`
game-control.tsx:1023 `const isBreakToggleDisabled = ... || isPausedForValidation;`
game-control.tsx:1025 `const isVoidLastNumberDisabled = ... || isPausedForValidation;`
The control pad (lines 1156-1214) renders only Next Number, Take Break, Check Claim, Undo Last Call and Winners & Prizes. `handleResumeGame` is wired only inside the validation modal (lines 1339 and 1397).
suggested_fix: Render a Resume button on the main pad (or repurpose the Take Break button) whenever `currentGameState.paused_for_validation` is true, calling `handleResumeGame`; alternatively correct the Post Win copy to name the Check Claim route.
verify_note: Verified: isNextNumberDisabled (1022), isBreakToggleDisabled (1023) and isVoidLastNumberDisabled (1025) all include isPausedForValidation, the control pad (1156-1214) renders no Resume, and handleResumeGame is wired only inside the validation modal (1339, 1397). The modal copy at 1783 does say 'Resume ... from the main pad'. But isValidateButtonDisabled (1024) deliberately omits isPausedForValidation, so Check Claim stays enabled and its Cancel button relabels to 'Cancel & Resume' when paused (1397) - a signposted two-tap route out, not a dead end. Misleading copy plus one extra tap, not a frozen app.

title: The host's `snowball_pots` realtime channel can never fire: the table is not in the publication
summary: `pot_updates_host:${pot_id}` subscribes to UPDATE events on `public.snowball_pots`, which is absent from `supabase_realtime`, so the host's jackpot figure is whatever was read at mount for the life of the page.
failure_scenario: An admin corrects the pot on `/admin/snowball` while the host page is open on a snowball game. The host's panel keeps showing the old jackpot amount and the old `current_max_calls`, so the "N calls left" countdown and the amount quoted in the Record Winner modal are both wrong until the host reloads. The server still derives the real values from the locked pot row, so no wrong payout is written, but the host reads the wrong number to the room.
evidence:
game-control.tsx:352-361:
```
potChannel = supabase
    .channel(`pot_updates_host:${game.snowball_pot_id}`)
    .on<SnowballPot>('postgres_changes', { event: 'UPDATE', schema: 'public', table: 'snowball_pots', filter: `id=eq.${game.snowball_pot_id}` }, (payload) => { setCurrentSnowballPot(payload.new); })
    .subscribe();
```
Live `pg_publication_tables` for `supabase_realtime`: game_states, game_states_public, sessions only.
suggested_fix: Re-read the pot alongside the existing 3-second `pollGameState` (or on the visibility handler), or add `public.snowball_pots` to the publication in a guarded migration.
verify_note: Live pg_publication_tables shows supabase_realtime carries only game_states, game_states_public and sessions, so the `pot_updates_host:` channel at game-control.tsx:352-361 can never fire, and the effect's mount fetch is the only writer of currentSnowballPot. The consequence is exactly as scoped: a stale jackpot figure and countdown read out to the room, with the server still deriving real values from the locked pot row inside record_winner_atomic and settle_snowball_pot, so no wrong payout is written. Also needs an admin editing the pot mid-game, which is rare. Low is right.

title: Skipping the final stage completes the game outside `endGame`: no `ended_at`, `sessions.active_game_id` still points at the finished game, and the host gets no next step
summary: `skipStage` (and the racy `newGameStatus === 'completed'` branch of `advanceToNextStage`) sets `status = 'completed'` directly, so it skips everything `endGame` does beyond the pot settlement: it never writes `ended_at`, never clears `sessions.active_game_id`, and the client never opens the Post Win modal or navigates.
failure_scenario: Game 2 of 5 reaches Full House and nobody claims by ball 90. The host opens Check Claim and taps "Skip (No Winner)". `skipStage` caps the index at the last stage and sets status completed. `maybeCompleteSession` finds games 3-5 incomplete, so the session stays 'running' with `active_game_id` still pointing at game 2. The TV at `/display/[sessionId]` keeps rendering the finished game 2 until the host separately starts game 3 from `/host`. On the host screen every control is now disabled, the validation modal has closed, no Post Win modal opens and no navigation happens, so the only way forward is the browser back arrow in the header. The `game_states.ended_at` for that game is left null, unlike every game ended through the Post Win path.
evidence:
actions.ts:1444-1467 (skipStage) writes only `current_stage_index`, `status`, `paused_for_validation` and the three display columns; no `ended_at`.
Compare actions.ts:781-789 (endGame): `status: 'completed', ended_at: new Date().toISOString(), ...` and actions.ts:815-834, which explicitly clears `active_game_id` when the session is not yet complete.
actions.ts:1476-1483 `if (newStatus === 'completed') { handleSnowballPotUpdate(...); maybeCompleteSession(...) }` — the pot and session-completion legs are there, the `ended_at` and `active_game_id` legs are not.
game-control.tsx:872-875 the client's success arm only closes the validation modal and clears the selection.
`grep -rn "active_game_id" src/` shows `/display/[sessionId]/page.tsx:69` and `/player/[sessionId]/page.tsx:51` both drive the public surfaces off `session.active_game_id`.
suggested_fix: Have `skipStage` and `advanceToNextStage` reuse the same completion tail as `endGame` (set `ended_at`, settle the pot, `maybeCompleteSession`, then clear `active_game_id` when the session stays running), and on the client open the Post Win / next-game prompt when the returned state comes back completed.
verify_note: The mechanism is real - skipStage (actions.ts:1452-1467) and the completed branch of advanceToNextStage (1180-1187) write status='completed' with no ended_at and never clear sessions.active_game_id, unlike endGame (781-834) - but the reviewer over-states the harm on all three legs. (1) ended_at: `grep -rn ended_at src/` shows it is only ever listed in select strings for display/player; no UI or report reads it, and live `count(*) filter (where status='completed' and ended_at is null)` on game_states is 0 across 60 rows. (2) active_game_id: it points at a game that genuinely just finished, and the pot settlement and maybeCompleteSession legs are both present, so no money or session-completion consequence. (3) 'only way forward is the browser back arrow': the game page renders its own header with a Link to /host (page.tsx:91-95), which is the same route the host uses after every other game end. What survives is a workflow gap - no Post Win modal, no navigation - which is polish rather than a live-game failure.

title: An inner modal unmounting releases the body scroll lock while the outer modal is still open
summary: `Modal` sets `document.body.style.overflow` from an effect whose cleanup unconditionally writes `"unset"`, so closing a stacked modal unlocks page scroll behind the modal that is still open.
failure_scenario: On the host screen the Record Winner modal is stacked over the still-open Validate Ticket modal. The host taps Cancel on Record Winner; its effect cleanup runs `document.body.style.overflow = "unset"`. The Validate Ticket modal is still open but the page behind it now scrolls under touch, so a mis-swipe on the 90-number grid scrolls the page instead of the grid.
suggested_fix: Use a module-level open-modal counter and only restore `overflow` when the count reaches zero.
verify_note: Read modal.tsx:77-85: the effect keys on isOpen and its cleanup unconditionally writes overflow='unset', so when the inner modal's isOpen flips false its cleanup runs while the outer modal's effect does not re-run - body scroll is released with a modal still open. The stacking is real on this screen (handleCloseRecordWinnerModal at 894 closes only showWinnerModal, leaving showValidationModal open; the comment at 1294 acknowledges the stack). Consequence is a mis-swipe scrolling the page behind the 90-number grid. Cosmetic, low.

title: p_force_snowball_jackpot bypasses the call-window check entirely, and the button that sets it is available to any host at any call count
summary: CLAUDE.md states "The window is re-checked inside `record_winner_atomic`, so an out-of-window jackpot cannot be awarded by the client." That is not what the function does: `if coalesce(p_force_snowball_jackpot,false) or (v_window_open and ...)` short-circuits on the force flag before the window is consulted. The Manual Snowball Win button passes `true` and is rendered for any snowball game with a pot, regardless of `numbers_called_count`.
failure_scenario: Snowball window is 48 calls; the pot is £200; ball 71 is called and a Full House is claimed. The eligibility panel correctly says "Jackpot is closed". The host instead taps Manual Snowball Win (still on screen), Confirm Snowball Win, and `record_winner_atomic` writes `is_snowball_jackpot = true, prize_given = true, prize_description = '£200.00 (Manual Snowball Win)'`. `settle_snowball_pot` then RESETS the pot to base. A host-role account, not an admin, has just paid and cleared a £200 pot outside the rules with two taps and no second approval. Any authenticated host can also do it directly: `record_winner_atomic` is EXECUTE-able by `authenticated` (confirmed by the live advisor output).
evidence:
Live `record_winner_atomic` — `if coalesce(p_force_snowball_jackpot, false) or (v_window_open and coalesce(p_snowball_eligible, false)) then v_is_jackpot := true; v_jackpot_amount := v_pot_amount; end if;`
src/app/host/[sessionId]/[gameId]/game-control.tsx:1215 — `{game.type === 'snowball' && currentSnowballPot && ( ...button... )}` with no window condition.
:1886 — `recordWinner(sessionId, gameId, 'Full House', prizeDescription, true, /* forceSnowballJackpot */ true, true, ...)`.
CLAUDE.md, "Win Detection" section, contradicts this.
suggested_fix: Either gate the force path on `profiles.role = 'admin'` inside `record_winner_atomic` (an override of the payout rules is a money decision), or require a typed reason recorded on the winner row, and hide the Manual Snowball Win button once the window is closed unless the user is an admin. Correct the CLAUDE.md claim either way.
verify_note: The live function confirms the short-circuit: `if coalesce(p_force_snowball_jackpot,false) or (v_window_open and coalesce(p_snowball_eligible,false))`, so the window is not consulted when force is set, and the Manual Snowball button (:1217) carries no window condition. So CLAUDE.md's 'an out-of-window jackpot cannot be awarded by the client' is inaccurate as written. But this is a deliberate override, not an oversight: the parameter is named p_force_snowball_jackpot, the call site is commented 'Force snowball jackpot override for manual award path', and the modal warns in bold that it will reset the pot and says it is for a missed automatic trigger or special circumstances. It is also the only recovery route for a missed eligibility tick. A host can already cause a pot reset in-window and can already record any prize text, so the marginal privilege is small. Severity corrected down to low: this is a doc/code mismatch to settle (gate the button on the window, or fix the CLAUDE.md sentence), not a security hole.

title: Money is displayed and stored with the last pence digit stripped: £212.50 renders as "£212.5"
summary: `formatPounds` does `value.toFixed(2).replace(/\.?0+$/, '')`, which strips a trailing zero from a two-decimal amount. The database does the same with `trim_scale(round(v_jackpot_amount,2))::text` when it builds the winner's prize text. Both are used on customer-facing surfaces.
failure_scenario: Admin sets `jackpot_increment` to 12.50 (or any amount with a 0 in the pence). The pot reaches 212.50. The pub TV (`display-ui.tsx:842`), the punters' phones (`player-ui.tsx:788`), the host screen (`game-control.tsx:1135`) and the pre-game briefing all show "£212.5". When the jackpot is won, `record_winner_atomic` writes `prize_description = 'Snowball Jackpot £212.5'` into the permanent winners record. Verified: `formatPounds(212.5) -> '212.5'`, `formatPounds(20.50) -> '20.5'`, and on the live database `trim_scale(round(212.50,2))::text -> '212.5'`.
evidence:
src/lib/snowball.ts:34-41 — `if (Number.isInteger(value)) return `${value}`; return value.toFixed(2).replace(/\.?0+$/, '');`
Live `record_winner_atomic` — `v_amount_text := trim_scale(round(v_jackpot_amount, 2))::text; v_jackpot_text := 'Snowball Jackpot £' || v_amount_text;` and `v_display_win_text := 'FULL HOUSE + SNOWBALL £' || v_amount_text || '!'`.
Call sites: src/app/display/[sessionId]/display-ui.tsx:842, :1060; src/app/player/[sessionId]/player-ui.tsx:788; src/app/host/[sessionId]/[gameId]/game-control.tsx:1135, :1671; src/components/host/pre-game-briefing.tsx:77; src/lib/jackpot.ts:31.
suggested_fix: Format money as either a whole number or exactly two decimals — never one. `Number.isInteger(v) ? String(v) : v.toFixed(2)`. In SQL use `to_char(round(v,2), 'FM999999990.00')` with the integer case handled explicitly, rather than `trim_scale`.
verify_note: Both halves reproduce. src/lib/snowball.ts:34-41: 212.50.toFixed(2) is '212.50' and /\.?0+$/ strips the trailing zero to '212.5'. On production, trim_scale(round(212.50,2))::text returns '212.5' (and 20.00 -> '20', 212.05 -> '212.05'), so the winners row and the display text inherit it. Severity corrected down from medium to low: this is presentation only. No amount changes, £212.5 is unambiguous to a reader, and nobody is paid the wrong sum, which is squarely the 'cosmetic' band.

title: The jackpot amount is dropped from the winner record whenever the planned prize text already contains the word "snowball"
summary: `record_winner_atomic` appends the jackpot text only when `position('snowball' in lower(v_prize)) = 0`. A perfectly ordinary admin-entered prize such as "£20 Snowball Full House" trips that check, so a genuine jackpot win is stored with the stage prize alone and the jackpot amount appears nowhere in the audit row.
failure_scenario: Admin sets the snowball game's Full House prize to "£20 Snowball Game". Pot is £140, window open, punter wins, host chooses Eligible. `v_prize` already contains "snowball", so the `' + Snowball Jackpot £140'` suffix is skipped. The `winners` row reads "£20 Snowball Game". The big screen flashes "FULL HOUSE + SNOWBALL £140!" and then clears, but the Winners & Prizes list the host pays from — and the permanent audit record — say £20. The punter is underpaid by £140 unless somebody remembers the flash.
evidence:
Live `record_winner_atomic`: `if v_prize is null then v_prize := v_jackpot_text; elsif position('snowball' in lower(v_prize)) = 0 then v_prize := v_prize || ' + ' || v_jackpot_text; end if;`
The host list renders `winner.prize_description` verbatim (src/app/host/[sessionId]/[gameId]/game-control.tsx:1452-1454), and `is_snowball_jackpot` is not shown there at all.
suggested_fix: Drop the substring heuristic and always append the jackpot text when `v_is_jackpot` is true (or key the de-duplication on the exact generated `v_jackpot_text`, not on the word "snowball"). Also render an explicit "+ JACKPOT £X" badge in the Winners & Prizes list from `is_snowball_jackpot` rather than relying on free text.
verify_note: The live function body matches the migration verbatim: the ' + Snowball Jackpot £x' suffix is skipped whenever position('snowball' in lower(v_prize)) <> 0, and the host list prints prize_description verbatim with no jackpot badge (game-control.tsx:1444-1454). But the check is not arbitrary: the Manual Snowball path sets the prize to '£140.00 (Manual Snowball Win)', which already carries the amount and would otherwise double up, which is what the guard is for. The bad case needs an admin to free-type 'snowball' into the stage prize; production's snowball game prize is '£10 Cash', so it has never fired. Severity corrected down to low: latent, dependent on admin free text, and the win still carries is_snowball_jackpot=true and the on-screen amount.

title: The snowball pot admin form silently resets a stored increment of 0 to the hard-coded default on the next save
summary: Every numeric field uses `defaultValue={editingPot?.X || <default>}`, which treats a stored 0 as absent. `calls_increment` and the max-calls fields are true integers over the wire (numeric money columns arrive as strings, e.g. `"20.00"`, so those are accidentally safe), so a pot deliberately configured with `calls_increment = 0` is silently rewritten to 2 the next time an admin opens and saves the pot.
failure_scenario: Admin configures the 2026 Snowball with a fixed 48-call window and `calls_increment = 0` — the pot grows in cash but the window never widens. Weeks later they open the pot to bump the jackpot amount; the Calls Increment field renders "2" instead of "0" and they save. From then on `settle_snowball_pot` widens the window by 2 calls every rollover, so the jackpot becomes progressively easier to win and gets paid out sooner and more often than the house intended. `updateSnowballPot` accepts it (`calls_increment: z.coerce.number().min(0)`) and writes it with no diff shown.
evidence:
src/app/admin/snowball/snowball-list.tsx:248 — `defaultValue={editingPot?.calls_increment || 2}`; :198 — `defaultValue={editingPot?.current_max_calls || 48}`; :222 — `defaultValue={editingPot?.base_max_calls || 48}`.
Live prod row confirms the wire types: `base_jackpot_amount: "20.00"` (string, truthy even at zero) vs `calls_increment: 2` (number).
src/app/admin/snowball/actions.ts:13-17 — the schema allows `calls_increment` down to 0, so 0 is a legal stored value.
suggested_fix: Use `??` instead of `||` for every `defaultValue` in this form: `editingPot?.calls_increment ?? 2`.
verify_note: The `|| default` pattern is there (snowball-list.tsx:198, 222, 248) and a stored calls_increment of 0 would render as 2. The reviewer's own wire-type point narrows this further than they said: the money columns arrive as strings ('20.00') so they are safe, and current_max_calls/base_max_calls are guarded by z.coerce.number().min(1) so a stored 0 is impossible there. calls_increment is the single affected field. Live pot '2026 Snowball' has calls_increment = 2, so nothing is currently at risk. Severity corrected down to low: it needs a deliberate 0 configuration, the wrong value is visible in the form before the admin saves, and it is one field.

title: set_winner_prize_given will mark a voided winner's prize as handed over
summary: The RPC checks the winner exists and belongs to the session, but not `is_void`. The host UI disables the button for voided rows (`disabled={... || winner.is_void === true}`), so the guard exists only on the client for a money-adjacent flag on a win that has been cancelled.
failure_scenario: A win is voided after the host already marked the prize given, or a stale host tab (whose `sessionWinners` list still shows `is_void: false`) posts `toggleWinnerPrizeGiven` for a row an admin has just voided. The RPC writes `prize_given = true` on a voided winner and returns true, so the action reports success. The session's paid-out record then shows a prize handed over against a cancelled win, which is exactly the row a cash reconciliation would trip over.
evidence:
Live `set_winner_prize_given`: `select session_id into v_session_id from public.winners where id = p_winner_id for update; if not found then raise exception 'winner_not_found'; end if; if v_session_id is distinct from p_session_id then raise exception 'wrong_session'; end if; update public.winners set prize_given = p_prize_given where id = p_winner_id returning prize_given into v_prize_given;` — no `is_void` test.
src/app/host/[sessionId]/[gameId]/game-control.tsx:1468 — `disabled={!canTogglePrize || winner.is_void === true}` (client-side only).
suggested_fix: Select `is_void` alongside `session_id` in the RPC and raise a mapped key (e.g. `winner_voided`) when it is true and `p_prize_given` is true. Add the mapping to HOST_RPC_ERRORS in src/app/host/actions.ts.
verify_note: Pulled the live definition: set_winner_prize_given calls assert_is_host(), locks the winners row, checks existence and session, then updates prize_given and returns the persisted value. There is no is_void test, so it will tick a voided win. The only guard is the client at game-control.tsx:1468. Real impact is small: it needs a stale host tab racing an admin void, or a hand-crafted call, and it leaves a prize_given flag on a row already stamped VOID in the same list, so a reconciliation sees both facts. Low is correct.

title: validateClaim accepts a claim made of the same number repeated, and rejects nothing about duplicates
summary: The server checks the array length against the per-stage required count, that every entry is an integer 1..90, that the last called ball is present, and that every entry is in the called set. It never de-duplicates, so `[7,7,7,7,7]` where 7 is the last called ball passes as a valid Line.
failure_scenario: The grid UI cannot produce duplicates, so this is not reachable by tapping — but `validateClaim` is a server action any authenticated host session can post to directly, and the whole point of the function is that the server does not trust the client's arithmetic. A malformed or replayed payload of five copies of the last ball returns `{valid: true}`, the host screen shows "Valid Claim", and a win is announced on the big screen for a ticket that does not exist. (Impact is capped because a host can record a winner without validating at all, so this is a correctness gap rather than a privilege escalation.)
evidence:
src/app/host/actions.ts:1029-1031 — `if (claimedNumbers.length !== requiredSelectionCount) { ... }` is the only cardinality check.
:1044-1050 — `for (const num of claimedNumbers) { if (!calledNumbersSet.has(num)) invalidNumbers.push(num) }` — set membership, so repeats all pass.
No `new Set(claimedNumbers).size` check anywhere in the function.
suggested_fix: Add `if (new Set(claimedNumbers).size !== claimedNumbers.length) return failure('validateClaim', 'A claim cannot repeat the same number.')` before the membership loop.
verify_note: Read the whole function (src/app/host/actions.ts:975-1057). The only cardinality test is length vs requiredSelectionCount at :1029, membership is a Set lookup at :1044-1050, and there is no new Set(claimedNumbers).size check anywhere, so [7,7,7,7,7] with 7 as the last ball returns valid:true. Reachable only by posting the action directly: the grid UI cannot produce duplicates. Impact is nil in practice, and lower than the finding implies: validateClaim writes nothing, the big-screen announcement is a separate announceWin call the host makes, and a host can record a winner without validating at all. Low is correct.

title: The narrow SELECT lists on the public pages give false comfort: the anon key shipped to those pages can read every column of games and sessions
summary: Four separate comments in the display and player code state that "Explicit narrow column lists keep public surfaces from leaking unintended fields". They do not: the live RLS on `games` and `sessions` is `SELECT ... to public USING (true)`, and RLS grants row access, not column access. Any punter who scans the QR gets the anon key from the page bundle and can read `games.notes`, `sessions.notes` and `sessions.created_by` directly.
failure_scenario: A guest opens devtools on /player/{id}, copies `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` out of the JS bundle, and issues `GET /rest/v1/sessions?select=*`. They receive every session ever run, including `notes` and the `created_by` staff user id. Today `notes` is empty on all six production rows, so nothing is actually exposed -- but the code comments actively discourage anyone from noticing that `notes` is a staff-only free-text field a member of staff could reasonably use for takings, prize float, or a note about a barred customer.
evidence: Live RLS (from the brief, re-confirmed against the policy list): `games | Read access for all | SELECT | to public | using true` and `sessions | Read access for all | SELECT | to public | using true`. Column list for `sessions` includes `notes text` and `created_by uuid`; `games` includes `notes text`. The misleading comment appears at display page.tsx:15-16, player page.tsx:14-15, display-ui.tsx:97-98 and player-ui.tsx:89-90. Verified `select count(*) filter (where notes is not null and notes <> '') from sessions` returns 0, so this is currently latent.
suggested_fix: Either move `notes` off the publicly readable tables, or replace the `using (true)` policies with column-restricted grants (`revoke select on public.sessions from anon; grant select (id, name, start_date, status, is_test_session, active_game_id) on public.sessions to anon;` and the equivalent for `games`), which is the only mechanism that actually enforces the column list. At minimum, correct the four comments so the next reader does not assume the narrow select is a security boundary.
verify_note: Verified live: anon holds SELECT on both `games` and `sessions`, RLS is `Read access for all | SELECT | to public | using true` on each, and `information_schema.columns` confirms `sessions.notes`, `sessions.created_by` and `games.notes` exist. RLS filters rows, not columns, so `GET /rest/v1/sessions?select=*` with the bundled anon key returns those fields — the narrow SELECT lists in the page code are documentation, not enforcement, and the four comments claiming they 'keep public surfaces from leaking unintended fields' are misleading. The exposure is not purely hypothetical either: `notes` is a live admin-editable free-text field wired to a form at src/app/admin/dashboard.tsx:238 and written by src/app/admin/actions.ts:46 and sessions/[id]/actions.ts:62, so staff can and eventually will type something into it. Low stands: it is currently empty on all six production rows, the data is operational rather than personal, and public row-level read on sessions/games is a deliberate requirement of the TV and follower screens.

title: The TV has no unattended path back to a live game: /display never re-checks for a new session and /display/[sessionId] is pinned to a completed one forever
summary: `/display` is a pure server component with no client-side refresh: when zero sessions are ready or running it renders a static "Waiting for the next game to start..." card whose only escape is a human clicking Refresh. And once a session completes, `/display/[sessionId]` locks into the terminal `completed` phase and never redirects back to `/display`, so a TV left on overnight shows the thank-you screen the next evening.
failure_scenario: Staff switch the TV on and open `/display` at 5pm, before the admin has created tonight's session. The production database currently holds six sessions, all `completed` and none `ready` (verified live), so the page falls to the empty branch at page.tsx:63-73. At 7pm the admin creates the session and the host starts game 1. The TV is still showing "No Active Games" -- there is no interval, no `router.refresh()`, no meta refresh and no realtime subscription on this route -- so a member of staff has to walk over and tap Refresh. The mirror case: the TV is left on `/display/{lastNightId}` overnight; `isSessionCompletedState` at display-ui.tsx:580 stays true, `loadPhase` resolves to 'completed' at :601 and the thank-you screen is terminal, so the same manual intervention is needed the following week.
evidence: src/app/display/page.tsx is `export default async function DisplayPage()` with no 'use client' child that refreshes; the only recovery affordance is `<Link href="/display"><Button variant="outline">Refresh</Button></Link>` at :69-71. Live query `select status, is_test_session, count(*) from sessions group by 1,2` returns a single row: `completed | false | 6`, confirming the zero-active-session state is the normal starting condition every night. display-ui.tsx:600-606 `if (isSessionCompletedState) return 'completed';` is the first and unconditional branch of `loadPhase`.
suggested_fix: Give `/display` a small client wrapper that calls `router.refresh()` on a 15-30 second interval while no session is active, and prefer a `running` session over a `ready` one when several match (today `sessions.length === 1` is the only auto-redirect condition, so one stale `ready` session will permanently break the redirect). On `/display/[sessionId]`, when `currentSession.status === 'completed'` and the poll sees another session become `running`, redirect to `/display` rather than sitting on the terminal screen.
verify_note: Both halves check out. src/app/display/page.tsx is a plain async server component with no client child, no `export const revalidate`, no meta refresh and no realtime subscription; the empty branch's only affordance is the `<Link href="/display">Refresh</Link>` at :69-71. Live query confirms all six production sessions are `completed | is_test_session=false`, so the zero-active-session state is genuinely the nightly starting condition. And display-ui.tsx:601 `if (isSessionCompletedState) return 'completed';` is the first, unconditional branch of loadPhase with nothing that navigates away, so a TV parked on last night's session id is terminal. I am dropping this to low: in both cases the recovery is one click by a member of staff who is standing in the room and already switching the TV on for the evening, no live game is interrupted, no money moves, and /display is by design a manually-pointed big screen rather than a kiosk. It is a nice ergonomic fix (poll for a ready/running session, redirect out of a completed one), not a guardrail gap that costs a bingo night.

title: The game-state realtime reconnect has no re-entrancy guard, so two concurrent connect() calls orphan a subscribed channel that is never removed
summary: `connect()` is async and awaits `removeChannel(activeChannel)` before nulling `activeChannel` and creating the replacement. It is invoked from two independent triggers -- the backoff `setTimeout` inside the subscribe callback and the `visibilitychange` handler via `reconnectGameStateRef` -- with no flag preventing overlap. When both run, the first one's freshly created channel is overwritten by the second and is left subscribed with no reference, so it is never torn down on cleanup.
failure_scenario: A guest's phone loses signal in the pub. The channel reports CHANNEL_ERROR and a 2-second backoff timer is armed (player-ui.tsx:325-327). The guest pockets the phone and takes it out again 2 seconds later; `visibilitychange` fires and calls `reconnectGameStateRef.current()` (player-ui.tsx:351) at almost the same moment the timer fires. Both `connect()` invocations read `activeChannel === C0`, both `await removeChannel(C0)` (the second is a no-op), then both proceed: connect#1 assigns `activeChannel = C1`, connect#2 assigns `activeChannel = C2`. C1 is subscribed to `game_states_public` but unreachable -- the effect cleanup at :341-342 only removes C2. Every call now delivers two payloads (two `setCurrentGameState` calls, two re-renders, two reveal-effect teardown/re-plan cycles per ball), and the leaked channel counts against the project's Realtime concurrent-connection budget for the rest of the evening. Repeat over a two-hour session with a flaky connection and the count grows monotonically.
evidence: display-ui.tsx:289-296 `const connect = async () => { if (!isMounted) return; if (activeChannel) { await supabaseClient.removeChannel(activeChannel); activeChannel = null; } if (!isMounted) return; ...` followed by :335 `activeChannel = channel;`. Triggers: :331 `reconnectTimer = setTimeout(() => { void connect(); }, delay);` and :338 `reconnectGameStateRef.current = () => { void connect(); };` consumed by the visibility effect at :352-359. Nothing serialises the two.
suggested_fix: Add a `let connecting = false;` (or a promise chain) inside each effect: `const connect = async () => { if (connecting || !isMounted) return; connecting = true; try { ... } finally { connecting = false; } }`. Also clear any armed `reconnectTimer` at the top of `connect()` so a visibility-triggered reconnect cancels the pending backoff rather than racing it.
verify_note: The interleaving is real: connect() reads `activeChannel`, awaits removeChannel, and only then nulls it (display-ui.tsx:289-296, player-ui.tsx:285-292), so two invocations that both start before the first await resolves each build a channel and the second overwrites the first's `activeChannel = channel` assignment (:335 / :331). The orphan stays subscribed and is never passed to removeChannel, including in the cleanup. Both triggers exist and are unserialised (backoff setTimeout at :331 and reconnectGameStateRef via visibilitychange at :338/:352). But the consequences are much smaller than claimed, so this is polish not a live-game risk: the leaked channel carries the same filter, and a duplicate payload is harmless — isFreshGameState allows equal state_version so setCurrentGameState re-applies an identical snapshot and the reveal effect re-plans, but planReveal is pure and derives its answer from lastCallAtMs / lastRevealAtRef, so re-planning is idempotent and no ball is skipped, duplicated or re-timed. Net cost is a few extra renders and a handful of orphaned channels per evening, well inside Supabase's per-client channel budget, all reclaimed on the next page load.

title: Backlog catch-up is uncapped: a client that falls behind trickles balls at 1.2s each and shows a wrong "current number" for up to a minute
summary: When more than one ball is outstanding, `planReveal` advances exactly one ball per `PUBLIC_MIN_DWELL_MS` (1200ms) with no upper bound on how far behind the client may be. Everything downstream -- the giant main number, the Recent Calls strip, "Total Calls", and the snowball "Calls Left" countdown -- is derived from `revealedCallCount`, so a lagging client displays a stale number as if it were the live call.
failure_scenario: The pub TV's connection stalls for 100 seconds (WebSocket dead, one poll hung -- see finding no-data-staleness-detector). The host calls 15 balls in that window. When data resumes, `serverCount - revealedCount = 15`, which takes branch 4 at reveal-queue.ts:81-86 and paces one ball every 1200ms. For the next ~20 seconds the TV's main ball and the `currentNumberDelayed` shown in the claim-check overlay (display-ui.tsx:943) are balls the host called well over a minute ago, while `Total Calls` at :1073 under-reports by up to 15. If a punter shouts BINGO during that window and the host pauses, `snapImmediately` rescues the overlay -- but until then the big screen is confidently wrong. Nothing in the plan lets it jump the queue.
evidence: src/lib/reveal-queue.ts:81-86 `if (serverCount - revealedCount > 1) { if (dwellWaitMs === 0) { return { revealCount: revealedCount + 1, nextTickInMs: minDwellMs }; } return { revealCount: revealedCount, nextTickInMs: dwellWaitMs }; }` -- no branch tests the size of the gap. `PUBLIC_MIN_DWELL_MS = 1200` (call-timing.ts:14). `const revealedCallCount = delayedNumbers.length;` (display-ui.tsx:577) with the comment stating this is what "every public counter must use". Note the deliberate `adoptRevealCount` shortcut at display-ui.tsx:92 exists for exactly this problem on mount, but is not applied to a mid-life backlog.
suggested_fix: Add a catch-up ceiling to `planReveal`, mirroring the existing `adoptRevealCount` policy: when `serverCount - revealedCount` exceeds a threshold (e.g. 4), jump straight to `serverCount - 1` and let the normal single-ball delay gate the newest ball. That preserves "the newest ball is never revealed early" while dropping the guarantee that no intermediate ball is individually displayed -- which is the right trade for a screen whose job is to show the current call, and it keeps the strip correct because the numbers are still all present in `delayedNumbers`.
verify_note: Mechanically true: reveal-queue.ts:81-86 tests only `serverCount - revealedCount > 1` and never the size of the gap, so catch-up runs at exactly one ball per PUBLIC_MIN_DWELL_MS (1200ms, call-timing.ts:14), and adoptRevealCount (display-ui.tsx:92) is applied only on mount or a game switch (:521-526), never to a mid-life backlog. Every public counter reads revealedCallCount (:577), so they all lag together. The severity is over-called, though, and the headline figure is wrong: the reviewer's own scenario is 15 balls behind, which clears in ~18 seconds, not 'up to a minute' (a minute needs ~50 balls, i.e. most of a 90-ball game missed). It is self-correcting because 1200ms per ball is far faster than the host's real calling rate; a BINGO shout sets paused_for_validation, which hits branch 2 (snapImmediately) and snaps the board to the server instantly, so a claim can never be checked against a lagging board; and the snowball 'Calls Left' badge is cosmetic, since jackpot eligibility is re-derived server-side inside record_winner_atomic. Net effect is a TV that is visibly behind the host for ~20 seconds after an outage and then correct.

title: Both public screens subscribe to snowball_pots changes, but that table is not in the realtime publication
summary: `supabase_realtime` contains only `game_states`, `game_states_public` and `sessions`. The `pot_updates` / `pot_updates_player` postgres_changes subscriptions on `snowball_pots` can never fire, so the jackpot amount and `current_max_calls` on both public screens are frozen at whatever was read when the active game last changed.
failure_scenario: An admin corrects the jackpot on /admin/snowball mid-session (say from £120 to £150 after a miscount). `settle_snowball_pot` or the admin update writes the new value. Neither the pub TV nor any guest phone ever sees it: the subscription is inert and the pot is only re-read inside the effect keyed on `currentActiveGame` (display-ui.tsx:494). The TV keeps advertising £120 in the countdown badge (:842) and the footer (:1060) until the host starts the next game. Guests are shown a jackpot figure that no longer matches the one the pub will pay.
evidence: `select p.pubname, c.relname from pg_publication p left join pg_publication_rel pr on pr.prpubid = p.oid left join pg_class c on c.oid = pr.prrelid` on ref bcmorqsgeumtmhvctvgu returns exactly: supabase_realtime/game_states, supabase_realtime/game_states_public, supabase_realtime/sessions, supabase_realtime_messages_publication/messages. `snowball_pots` is absent. The code at display-ui.tsx:474-483 subscribes `{ event: 'UPDATE', schema: 'public', table: 'snowball_pots', filter: 'id=eq....' }` and the in-code comment claims "The pot is re-read whenever the active game changes" -- which is true, and is in fact the only mechanism that works.
suggested_fix: Pick one and make it honest. Either add `snowball_pots` to the `supabase_realtime` publication (it is already anon-SELECTable per the live RLS, so the payloads carry nothing new), or delete the two dead subscriptions and re-read the pot on the existing 3-second poll so the displayed jackpot is never more than a few seconds stale.
verify_note: Independently reproduced against production ref bcmorqsgeumtmhvctvgu: `select p.pubname, c.relname from pg_publication p left join pg_publication_rel pr ... left join pg_class c ...` returns exactly supabase_realtime/{game_states, game_states_public, sessions} and supabase_realtime_messages_publication/messages. snowball_pots is absent, so the postgres_changes subscriptions at display-ui.tsx:474-483 and player-ui.tsx:374 can never deliver a payload and the pot figure only moves when the effect's `currentActiveGame` dependency changes. CLAUDE.md's deployment note names only game_states_public as needing Realtime, so this is dead code rather than a broken feature. Low is right: a mid-session pot correction is rare, the stale figure is advertising only, and the amount actually paid is derived server-side inside settle_snowball_pot from the locked pot row, never from what the TV displayed. Worth deleting the subscription or adding the table to the publication, either way.

title: There is no way to export the record of a night: /admin/backup exports nothing and shows the planned draw order, not what was called
summary: The page documented as the export tool renders an unpaginated HTML list of every game's pre-generated number_sequence. It has no download, no CSV/JSON, no winners, no called numbers and no pot data, so the permanent record cannot leave the system.
failure_scenario: The licensee asks for the record of the 29 July night to file, or the app is being decommissioned and the six nights of history need archiving. /admin/backup is the only thing resembling an export. It lists number_sequence - the shuffled 1..90 array generated at start time, i.e. the planned draw order, not the balls actually called (called_numbers, which is a different column) - for every game ever created, currently 60 games at 90 numbers each in one unpaginated page, with no winners, no times, no prizes and no pot movements. There is no download control anywhere in the app. The only route to a permanent record is direct database access. As a side effect the page also renders the full future draw order for games that have not been played yet.
evidence: src/app/admin/backup/page.tsx:30-40 selects `id, game_index, name, game_states:game_states (number_sequence), sessions:sessions (name, start_date)` from games with no session filter and no limit, and lines 63-70 map game_states.number_sequence into spans. There is no <a download>, no Response with a Content-Disposition header, and no route handler producing CSV or JSON anywhere in src/app. Production holds 60 games. number_sequence is written once by generateShuffledNumberSequence() in src/app/host/actions.ts:204-212 and never mutated; the balls actually drawn live in called_numbers.
suggested_fix: Add a real per-session export (CSV or JSON) covering winners with their status and prize, each game's called_numbers with started_at/ended_at, and the pot movements for the night. Scope the existing backup call sheet to a single session, and consider hiding the sequence for games that have not started.
verify_note: Facts verified: admin/backup/page.tsx:30-40 selects games with number_sequence and session name, no session filter and no limit (60 games live), renders them as spans at 63-70, and grep finds no <a download>, no Content-Disposition and no CSV/JSON route anywhere in src/. Confirmed from the migration comments that number_sequence is the pre-drawn 90-ball order and called_numbers is what was actually drawn, so the page does show the planned order. Two corrections. The page is titled 'Backup Call Sheets' and reads as a paper fallback for when the app dies, which is a legitimate purpose - it is CLAUDE.md's route table calling it an 'Export tool' that is inaccurate, not the page. And the 'renders the full future draw order for unplayed games' aside is wrong: number_sequence is generated in startGame, so a never-started game has no game_states row and the page prints 'No number sequence generated'. Severity corrected from medium to low: a missing export feature, with the data intact and reachable by the sole admin through Supabase.

title: Controller handovers overwrite in place, so who was running the game at any moment is unrecoverable
summary: takeControl and startGame both overwrite game_states.controlling_host_id with the new host's id. Only the final controller survives, and nothing records that a takeover happened or when.
failure_scenario: Two staff run the night from two phones; the first phone's battery dies mid Game 6, the second host taps 'Take control' and finishes the session. The following week a win from Game 6 is disputed. game_states.controlling_host_id now holds only the second host's id (and winners rows hold no actor at all - see the winners finding), so 'who was in control when this ball was called and this win recorded?' has no answer. A stale-heartbeat takeover is indistinguishable from a deliberate one, and a takeover that happened by accident (a host opening the page on a second device) is indistinguishable from both.
evidence: src/app/host/actions.ts:520-545 (takeControl) does a single conditional `.update({ controlling_host_id, controller_last_seen_at })` on game_states with an `.or(...)` of the takeover conditions; there is no insert. src/app/host/actions.ts:385-395 (startGame) does the same via the service-role client for the in_progress branch. Live game_states holds a single controlling_host_id column and pg_trigger shows no audit trigger on the table.
suggested_fix: Log the handover into the same game_events table proposed for voided balls: game_id, event_type 'controller_taken', previous controller, new controller, whether the previous heartbeat was stale, and the timestamp.
verify_note: Code is as described: takeControl (host/actions.ts:523-562) is a single conditional .update() of controlling_host_id + controller_last_seen_at with no insert, startGame does the same for the in_progress branch, and there is no audit trigger on game_states. But the failure scenario cannot occur in production as it stands: auth.users holds exactly one row and profiles holds exactly one row (role admin), so 'two staff on two phones' would be the same user id, takeControl would match its own `controlling_host_id.eq.<self>` arm, and there would be nothing to distinguish. Severity corrected from medium to low: a latent gap that only bites once a second staff account exists.

title: deleteSnowballPot permanently destroys the pot's entire audit trail before deleting the pot
summary: The delete path removes every snowball_pot_history row for the pot, unlinks the pot from all historical games, then deletes the pot - and records nothing about any of it.
failure_scenario: An admin retires the '2026 Snowball' pot at the end of the year and creates a 2027 one. The action deletes all snowball_pot_history rows for the old pot, sets games.snowball_pot_id = null on every game that ever used it (including completed games from six past sessions), then deletes the pot row. Afterwards there is no record that the pot ever existed, no record of the £120 that accreted into it, no record of which games were snowball games, and no record that the deletion happened or who did it. The question 'what did the 2026 snowball pay out over the year?' becomes unanswerable, and past sessions silently lose the fact that Game 9 was a snowball game at all. Today this is masked only because snowball_pot_history is already empty; it becomes destructive the moment settlements start writing rows.
evidence: src/app/admin/snowball/actions.ts:155-181: "await supabase.from('games').update({ snowball_pot_id: null }).eq('snowball_pot_id', id)" then "await supabase.from('snowball_pot_history').delete().eq('snowball_pot_id', id)" then "await supabase.from('snowball_pots').delete().eq('id', id)". No audit insert anywhere in the function, and the comment says the history delete exists 'to satisfy FK constraints if cascade isn't configured'.
suggested_fix: Do not delete pots. Add an `archived_at` column and hide archived pots from the game-linking dropdown, leaving the history and the games.snowball_pot_id links intact. If deletion must stay, refuse it when any history row or any game reference exists.
verify_note: Read deleteSnowballPot (admin/snowball/actions.ts:134-185). It guards only against in_progress games, then nulls games.snowball_pot_id for every game ever linked, deletes every snowball_pot_history row for the pot, deletes the pot, and records nothing. The 'to satisfy FK constraints if cascade isn't configured' comment is there as quoted. Severity corrected from medium to low: with snowball_pot_history empty and one pot live, nothing is destroyed today, and the reviewer concedes as much. It is a latent hazard that matters only once settlement rows start accumulating - at which point the same fix (block or archive rather than delete) covers it.

title: game_states.updated_at never advances after insert, and the stale value is mirrored to public clients
summary: bump_game_state_version sets only state_version and no write path sets updated_at, so the column keeps the row's creation time forever while the row is updated hundreds of times. sync_game_states_public copies the stale value into game_states_public.
failure_scenario: Debugging the morning after: 'Game 10 stopped responding, when was it last touched?' The live row for 'Game 10 - Green (JACKPOT)' says updated_at = 2026-07-29 20:17:59.974766+00. Its state_version is 133 (133 updates) and its ended_at is 2026-07-30 06:24:17 - the next morning. Anyone reading updated_at concludes nothing happened to that row after 20:17 on the 29th, which is wrong by ten hours and 133 writes. The same wrong value is selected into the display and player payloads (GAME_STATE_PUBLIC_SELECT includes updated_at in all four files), so it is on the wire to public clients too. Separately, that 06:24 ended_at is itself a night that cannot be explained: nothing records why or by whom a game was ended ten hours after its last ball.
evidence: Live pg_get_functiondef(bump_game_state_version): "if tg_op = 'UPDATE' then new.state_version := coalesce(old.state_version, 0) + 1; end if; return new;" - updated_at is never touched. Column default is now() on insert only. Live row sample: {updated_at: 2026-07-29 20:17:59.974766+00, started_at: 2026-07-29 20:17:59.911+00, ended_at: 2026-07-30 06:24:17.048261+00, last_call_at: 2026-07-29 20:26:31.474+00, state_version: 133, status: completed}. Every sampled row shows updated_at within 60ms of started_at. sync_game_states_public copies `new.updated_at` verbatim into game_states_public.
suggested_fix: Set `new.updated_at := now()` in bump_game_state_version alongside the version bump. Also note the mixed clocks in the same rows: started_at and ended_at are Node's `new Date().toISOString()` from the server action while last_call_at is Postgres now(), so cross-column timing arithmetic is already approximate.
verify_note: Verified live on both halves. bump_game_state_version sets only state_version. Every game_states row for the July 29th session has updated_at within ~60-260ms of started_at while state_version runs 99-190, and Game 10 - Green shows updated_at 2026-07-29 20:17:59.97 against ended_at 2026-07-30 06:24:17 - the column is off by ten hours and 133 writes exactly as described. sync_game_states_public copies new.updated_at verbatim, and all four display/player select lists include it. Severity corrected from medium to low: nothing in the app reads it for ordering (the documented state_version comparator is used throughout, and grep finds no consumer of updated_at outside the four select strings), so the only harm is a column that lies to whoever debugs the morning after.

title: Winner History renders dates in the server's timezone and locale, with no time of day
summary: A server component formats winners.created_at with raw new Date(...).toLocaleDateString(), so on Vercel it renders in UTC with the Node default (US) locale, and the time of day is dropped entirely.
failure_scenario: A win recorded at 00:30 London time (BST, = 23:30 UTC the previous day) is listed under the previous date, so it appears on the wrong night. Everyday rows render as '7/29/2026' rather than 29/07/2026 for a British pub. Because only the date is shown and there is no session grouping or ordering hint beyond created_at desc, the order in which wins happened within a night is not visible on the page at all - the sibling session-detail page uses toLocaleString() and, being a client component, at least renders in the viewer's timezone.
evidence: src/app/admin/history/page.tsx is `export default async function HistoryPage()` with no 'use client', so line 91's `{new Date(winner.created_at).toLocaleDateString()}` executes in the Node runtime, which defaults to UTC and en-US on Vercel. src/app/admin/sessions/[id]/session-detail.tsx:365 uses toLocaleString() but that file starts with "use client". No dateUtils module or Europe/London reference exists anywhere in src/ (grep returns nothing).
suggested_fix: Format with an explicit locale and timezone (en-GB, Europe/London) and include the time, or move the formatting into a small client component so it renders in the viewer's timezone as session-detail already does.
verify_note: admin/history/page.tsx is an async server component with no 'use client', and line 91 is `{new Date(winner.created_at).toLocaleDateString()}`, so it formats in the Node runtime's timezone and locale rather than the viewer's; session-detail.tsx:365 uses toLocaleString() but that file is 'use client'. No dateUtils or Europe/London reference exists in src/. Severity low is correct, and the practical exposure is smaller than described: a pub bingo night ends well before midnight (the July 29th session's last ball was 20:26 UTC), so the date-shift case needs a win after 01:00 BST. The everyday harm is US-format dates and no time of day on the cross-session record.

title: snowball_pot_history is written but never read: no UI anywhere shows how the pot got to its current value
summary: The only money audit table in the schema has no reader. Nothing in src/ selects from snowball_pot_history; the admin snowball page shows the pot's current values and an edit form and nothing else.
failure_scenario: An admin wants to answer 'the jackpot says £140, show me the six £20 increments and who authorised them'. /admin/snowball renders SnowballList from the snowball_pots rows only. /admin/history renders winners only. There is no page, no export and no query in the app that reads snowball_pot_history, so even once rows start being written by settle_snowball_pot they are invisible to every user of the system. Answering the question requires direct SQL access to the production database.
