evidence: grep -rn 'snowball_pot_history' src/ returns only type definitions (src/types/database.ts), comments, and three writes/deletes in src/app/admin/snowball/actions.ts (lines 116, 166, 243). There is no `.from('snowball_pot_history').select(` anywhere in the codebase.
suggested_fix: Add a pot-history panel to /admin/snowball: change_type, old and new values, the linked game and session, changed_by resolved to an email, and created_at. It is the only way an admin can ever see the audit trail the system is now paying to write.
verify_note: grep confirms it: the only occurrences of snowball_pot_history in src/ are the type definitions, one comment in host/actions.ts:240, and the three writes/deletes in admin/snowball/actions.ts (116, 166, 243). There is no `.from('snowball_pot_history').select(` anywhere. /admin/snowball/page.tsx selects only from snowball_pots and renders SnowballList; /admin/history selects only winners. Severity corrected from high to low: this is a missing report, not a defect - nothing breaks, no user is misled, the table is currently empty anyway, and the sole admin has the Supabase dashboard. It becomes worth building once settlements start writing rows.

title: A refused bingo claim is stored nowhere: false calls leave no evidence the host checked
summary: validateClaim reads the called set server-side, computes invalidNumbers, returns them to the browser and stores nothing. The genuinely-invalid branch does not even log.
failure_scenario: A punter shouts BINGO, the host pauses, types the six numbers, and the server finds two of them were never called. The action returns { success: true, data: { valid: false, invalidNumbers: [12, 63] } }. The host says 'sorry, not a valid claim' and resumes. Nothing is written to any table and nothing is logged (the `return { success: true, data: { valid: false ... } }` path at line 1051 never calls logActionFailure; only the malformed-input arms do). The questions 'how many false claims did we have on the night?', 'was this the same table shouting three times?' and, crucially, 'did the host actually check the claim before refusing/paying?' cannot be answered from anything the system stores. The only claims that leave a trace are the ones that were paid.
evidence: src/app/host/actions.ts:1032-1055: the function computes invalidNumbers against calledNumbersSet and ends with "if (invalidNumbers.length > 0) { return { success: true, data: { valid: false, invalidNumbers } }; } else { return { success: true, data: { valid: true } }; }". No insert, no logActionFailure on either branch. There is no claims or claim_attempts table in the schema.
suggested_fix: Record every claim check: game_id, stage, call_count at the time, the claimed numbers, the verdict, the actor and the timestamp. The claimed numbers are already server-visible and contain nothing player-identifying, and having them stored is what would let a disputed win be reconstructed at all (today not even a successful claim stores which numbers were on the book).
verify_note: Read validateClaim (host/actions.ts:980-1055) in full. It re-reads called_numbers server-side, enforces the stage's required count and the last-called-number rule, then returns { valid:false, invalidNumbers } with no insert and no logActionFailure on either terminal branch. There is no claims table in the schema (public tables are only game_states, game_states_public, games, profiles, sessions, snowball_pot_history, snowball_pots, winners). Severity corrected from medium to low: this is a feature that was never built rather than a broken one. No money is at risk, the live game is unaffected, and the refusal itself is server-validated and correct.

title: Session completion writes no timestamp and does not check the write landed
summary: maybeCompleteSession and updateSessionStatus both flip sessions.status with a bare .update() - no .select(), no rowcount check, and sessions has no ended_at or completed_at column.
failure_scenario: The last game of the night ends; maybeCompleteSession writes status 'completed' and active_game_id null. If that update matches nothing (RLS, stale id) it returns no error and no rows and the function simply returns, leaving the session showing as running with no error anywhere. When it does succeed, no timestamp is stored, so 'what time did the night finish?' is only derivable from max(game_states.ended_at) - which production shows can be misleading: the July 29th session's last game carries ended_at 2026-07-30 06:24:17, ten hours after its final ball, because someone ended it the next morning and nothing records that.
evidence: src/app/host/actions.ts:296-300: "await supabase.from('sessions').update({ status: 'completed', active_game_id: null }).eq('id', sessionId)" - the result is not even destructured. src/app/admin/sessions/[id]/actions.ts:309-316 has the same shape with only an `if (error)` check. information_schema.columns for sessions: id, name, start_date, notes, status, is_test_session, created_by, created_at, active_game_id - no ended_at, completed_at or updated_at.
suggested_fix: Add .select('id') and treat zero rows as a failure in both places, and add a completed_at column set when the status moves to 'completed' so the night has an authoritative end time independent of the last game's ended_at.
verify_note: maybeCompleteSession (host/actions.ts:297-302) does not even destructure the result of the sessions .update(), and updateSessionStatus (sessions/[id]/actions.ts:304-320) checks only `if (error)` with no .select(). Live sessions columns confirm no ended_at/completed_at/updated_at: id, name, start_date, notes, status, is_test_session, created_by, created_at, active_game_id. Also confirmed the supporting oddity - Game 10 of the July 29th session carries ended_at 2026-07-30 06:24:17 against a last_call_at of 20:26 the night before. Severity low is right: the session's completion state is cosmetic bookkeeping, a stuck 'running' session is visible on /admin and fixable by the admin status control, and no money or live-game path depends on it.

title: /api/setup grants the admin role with no audit, no logging, and without proving the write landed
summary: The bootstrap endpoint updates profiles.role to 'admin' using the service-role client with no .select(), no audit row, no log line, and profiles has no updated_at, so a privilege escalation to admin is invisible after the fact.
failure_scenario: Two problems from one call. (1) The write is unverified: `.update({ role: 'admin' }).eq('id', user.id)` with no .select(). If the profiles row does not exist (the auth-user trigger failed, or the user predates it) the update matches zero rows, PostgREST returns no error, and the endpoint responds `{ success: true, user: <email>, role: 'admin' }` while nothing was written. The operator believes the account is admin; the next login is refused as a non-admin and nobody knows why. This is exactly the failure pattern CLAUDE.md documents as having already bitten the prize tick and the snowball pot. (2) Even when it does land, nothing records it: profiles has only id/role columns with no updated_at, there is no audit table, and the route logs nothing on success. Answering 'when did this account become admin, and who ran the setup call?' is impossible. Production currently holds exactly one profile row, so an unexpected second admin would be the only signal.
evidence: src/app/api/setup/route.ts:91-100: "const { error: updateError } = await supabase.from('profiles').update({ role: 'admin' }).eq('id', user.id); if (updateError) { ... } return NextResponse.json({ success: true, user: user.email, role: 'admin' })". No .select(), no rowcount check, no logging. `select count(*) from profiles` returns 1. profiles has no updated_at column.
suggested_fix: Add `.select('id')` and treat zero rows as a 500, and emit a logActionFailure/console line on both success and failure recording the target email (already in the request) and the timestamp so the grant is at least visible in the Vercel log.
verify_note: The code is exactly as quoted (route.ts:91-100): a service-role .update({role:'admin'}).eq('id', user.id) with no .select(), no rowcount check, no logging, and profiles has no updated_at (live columns: id, email, role, created_at - note the reviewer's 'only id/role' is slightly wrong but the point survives). Sub-claim (1) is weaker than stated: the on_auth_user_created trigger on auth.users runs handle_new_user, which inserts the profiles row for every user at creation, so the zero-row case needs a user predating the trigger or a failed insert. Severity corrected from medium to low: it is a one-shot bootstrap endpoint behind SETUP_SECRET, run by the operator on themselves, and a failure to land surfaces at the very next login. The unverified-write pattern still violates the CLAUDE.md invariant and should be tidied.

title: A voided ball is erased with no record of which number, when, or by whom
summary: void_last_number pops the last element out of called_numbers and decrements the count in place. The number that was voided, the time, and the host who did it are all discarded, and last_call_at is deliberately left untouched so even the timing signal is lost.
failure_scenario: During Game 6 a host mis-taps and calls a ball early, then voids it. The ball goes back in the bag and is re-drawn later. A punter afterwards says 'you called 47, then said you hadn't, and then called it again ten minutes later'. The only stored artefacts are the final called_numbers array and a state_version counter. Nothing records that a void happened, which number, at what time, or by which host, so the claim cannot be checked either way. The same applies to the display_win_type/display_win_text/display_winner_name that the void clears: a win announcement that went up on the big screen and was then withdrawn leaves no trace.
evidence: Live pg_get_functiondef(void_last_number): "update public.game_states set called_numbers = coalesce(called_numbers, '[]'::jsonb) - (v_length - 1), numbers_called_count = coalesce(numbers_called_count, 0) - 1, display_win_type = null, display_win_text = null, display_winner_name = null where game_id = p_game_id returning * into v_state;" - no insert anywhere, and last_call_at is not written. src/app/host/actions.ts:1500-1514 calls the RPC and logs only on failure (logActionLatency on success).
suggested_fix: Insert a row into a small game_events table (game_id, event_type 'ball_voided', number, actor auth.uid(), now()) inside the same transaction as the update. That one table would also cover controller takeovers and refused claims, which have the same problem.
verify_note: Live void_last_number matches the quote: it pops the last jsonb element, decrements the count, clears the three display_* columns, and inserts nothing; last_call_at is untouched (deliberately, per CLAUDE.md, so the host gap is not reset). src/app/host/actions.ts:1489-1514 calls the RPC and only logs on failure. Severity corrected from medium to low: nothing about the game is wrong, no money moves, and the only consequence is that a he-said-she-said about a mis-called ball cannot be settled from stored data. That is a nice-to-have call log, not a guardrail gap.

title: Every entrance animation class in the app is dead: no plugin provides animate-in / fade-in / zoom-in / slide-in-from-*, verified absent from the built CSS
summary: 30 usages of tailwindcss-animate class names across src/ compile to nothing, so the modal, win overlay, waiting screen and active-ball transitions are hard cuts rather than the intended fades.
failure_scenario: The win overlay is meant to fade up over the TV (`animate-in fade-in duration-300`); it actually pops instantly, as does every modal on the host's phone. `animate-bounce-slight` on the BingoBall 'active' variant does nothing at all. The intent is invisible in review because the class names read as if they work.
evidence: `grep -rn "tailwindcss-animate|tw-animate|keyframes|bounce-slight" package.json tailwind.config.ts src/app/globals.css` returns nothing; tailwind.config.ts has `plugins: []` and no keyframes; node_modules has no animate package. The built stylesheet .next/static/chunks/366f72b19d27c821.css contains 0 occurrences of `animate-in` and only three keyframes: bounce, pulse, spin. 30 usages across src/ (`grep -rno "animate-in|animate-bounce-slight|fade-in|zoom-in|slide-in-from" src/ | wc -l`).
suggested_fix: Either add `tw-animate-css` and import it in globals.css, or strip the dead classes and write the two or three transitions that matter (win overlay, modal) as plain CSS in globals.css alongside the existing mask utilities.
verify_note: Verified independently against the built stylesheet. package.json has no tailwindcss-animate or tw-animate dependency, tailwind.config.ts has plugins: [] and no keyframes, and globals.css defines no animation utilities. In .next/static/chunks/366f72b19d27c821.css, 'animate-in' occurs 0 times, 'bounce-slight' 0 times, and the only keyframes present are bounce, pulse and spin. So every animate-in / fade-in / zoom-in / slide-in-from-* / animate-bounce-slight usage in src/ is inert, including the win overlay (display-ui.tsx:1021) and every modal. Cosmetic only, and low is the right call.

title: Geist Sans is loaded and preloaded but never applied; body falls back to Arial
summary: layout.tsx configures Geist Sans as a CSS variable and tailwind.config maps font-sans to it, but globals.css sets an unlayered body font-family of Arial and nothing in src/ ever uses the font-sans class.
failure_scenario: Every visitor, including punters on pub wifi loading /player on a phone, downloads a Geist Sans woff2 that no element ever renders in. The whole app renders in Arial, so the typography of the TV numerals and headings is not what the config says it is.
evidence: layout.tsx:6-10 declares `geistSans` with `variable: "--font-geist-sans"`, applied on `<body>` at line 28. tailwind.config.ts maps `sans: ["var(--font-geist-sans)", "sans-serif"]`. globals.css:21-25 `body { color: ...; background: ...; font-family: Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif; }`, confirmed in the built CSS: `body{color:var(--foreground);background:var(--background);font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif}`. `grep -rn "font-sans" src/` returns nothing (font-mono is used 9 times, so Geist Mono is genuinely in play).
suggested_fix: Either drop the Arial declaration and let the Tailwind font-sans default apply, or drop the Geist Sans import from layout.tsx so it is not fetched.
verify_note: Verified in the built output. layout.tsx:6-10 declares Geist with variable --font-geist-sans and applies it to <body> (line 28), tailwind.config.ts maps sans to it, but globals.css:21-25 sets body { font-family: Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif }, and the built CSS contains both 'font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif' for body and a @font-face family 'Geist'. grep for 'font-sans' across src/ returns nothing, while font-mono appears in six files, so Geist Mono is genuinely used and Geist Sans is downloaded for nothing. Low.

title: The host dashboard's Start button has no in-flight state or double-tap guard, and reports errors through window.alert / window.confirm
summary: The first action of the night gives no feedback while it is in flight, and the surrounding error and confirm handling uses blocking native dialogs that the live host screen deliberately replaced with modals.
failure_scenario: Host taps "Start" on pub wifi. The button does not change, no spinner appears, and the router.push does not fire for two or three seconds, so the host taps again. Two startGame calls go out. When one fails, the failure arrives as a native alert() box, which iOS will suppress after repeated dialogs ("Don't show more alerts"), leaving later failures completely silent.
evidence: Line 34 `const startSelectedGame = async (...)` with no isStarting state; the Button at 164-186 has no `disabled` or loading label and its onClick just awaits. Line 37 `alert("Error starting game: " + ...)`, line 181 `alert("An unexpected error occurred: " ...)`, line 256 `alert('Enter a cash jackpot amount first.')`, line 173 `confirm("⚠️ Are you sure you want to RE-OPEN this finished game?...")`. game-control.tsx line 97 records the opposite decision for the live screen: "Undo confirm modal (T4.3): replaces the blocking window.confirm."
suggested_fix: Add a per-game in-flight flag that disables the button and shows "Starting…", and replace the three alerts and the re-open confirm with the existing Modal + inline error-banner pattern used on the game control screen.
verify_note: The facts hold: startSelectedGame (dashboard.tsx:34) has no in-flight state, the Start button (164-186) has no disabled or loading label, and errors go through alert() at lines 37 and 181, with confirm() at 173 and alert() at 256. Correcting severity down to low: the harm claimed does not follow. startGame is defensively guarded server-side. Every branch binds its update to the status it read ('in_progress', 'completed', 'not_started') and returns a conflict rather than acting, and the destructive fresh-start path explicitly refuses to wipe a board another request already filled (actions.ts:385-470). So a double tap produces a confusing alert, never a corrupted or restarted game. What remains is a missing spinner and inconsistent dialog style on a screen used once per game, which is polish.

title: Login fields carry no autoComplete attributes
summary: The email and password inputs omit autoComplete, so password managers and iOS/Android autofill are less reliable on the one screen a stand-in host must get through before they can do anything.
failure_scenario: A stand-in host opens /login on a pub tablet. Safari's saved-password suggestion does not appear above the keyboard because the fields are not annotated, so they type an email and password they half-remember while the room waits.
evidence: Lines 71-78 `<Input id="email" name="email" type="email" placeholder="Enter email" required .../>` and lines 85-92 `<Input id="password" name="password" type="password" ... />` -- neither passes autoComplete.
suggested_fix: Add `autoComplete="username"` (or "email") and `autoComplete="current-password"`.
verify_note: Confirmed: login/page.tsx:71-78 and 85-92 pass id, name, type, placeholder and required, and components/ui/input.tsx spreads props with no autoComplete default, so neither field carries the attribute. Low, and the failure text overstates it: Safari and Chrome password managers autofill type=email / type=password fields heuristically from name and label even without autocomplete hints, so the saved-credential prompt usually still appears. Adding autoComplete="username" / "current-password" is a correctness improvement, not a blocker.

title: Buttons nested inside Links in nine places produce invalid, doubly-focusable markup
summary: `<Link><Button/></Link>` puts a <button> inside an <a>, which is invalid HTML and gives assistive technology two nested interactive elements for one target.
failure_scenario: A keyboard user tabbing the home page role picker stops twice per option (once on the anchor, once on the button) and hears the role announced ambiguously. Some screen readers skip the link name entirely and read only the button.
evidence: `grep -rn -B1 "<Button" src/app | grep -c "<Link"` returns 9. Examples: src/app/page.tsx:33-38, src/app/admin/dashboard.tsx:170-174, src/app/display/page.tsx:69-71, src/app/host/[sessionId]/[gameId]/page.tsx:91-95.
suggested_fix: Use `<Link className={buttonClasses}>` directly, or add an `asChild`-style prop to Button so it can render as the anchor.
verify_note: Reproduced the count: 9 occurrences of <Link> immediately wrapping <Button> across src/app (page.tsx x3, admin/dashboard.tsx, admin/sessions/[id]/page.tsx, admin/snowball/page.tsx, admin/history/page.tsx, display/page.tsx, host/[sessionId]/[gameId]/page.tsx), and components/ui/button.tsx renders a real <button>. Interactive content inside <a> is invalid HTML and the parser does not fix it up, so both elements stay focusable and each pair is two tab stops. Clicks still work (the event bubbles to the anchor), so this is a validity and AT-verbosity issue only. Low.

title: No prefers-reduced-motion handling anywhere, with indefinite pulsing on the public screens
summary: animate-pulse runs indefinitely on the TV's pre-call prize rows, the promo headline, the player's Checking Claim card and the host's ON BREAK banner, with no reduced-motion opt-out and no way for a viewer to stop it.
failure_scenario: A guest with vestibular sensitivity opens /player and hits a claim check: the whole card pulses continuously with no way to stop it. The TV's stage-and-prize panel pulses three rows on staggered delays for the entire pre-call period, which can be several minutes. WCAG 2.2.2 requires a pause/stop/hide mechanism for content that moves for more than five seconds.
evidence: `grep -rn "prefers-reduced-motion|motion-reduce" src/ tailwind.config.ts` finds only a comment (display-ui.tsx:814) noting that the snowball badge is static "so it needs no prefers-reduced-motion opt-out", i.e. the concern is known and unimplemented elsewhere. Indefinite pulses: display-ui.tsx:993 (`animate-pulse` per prize row with `animationDelay`), 986, 663 (servicePromoTitleClass), 1012 (READY...); player-ui.tsx:728, 710 (animate-bounce); game-control.tsx:1072, 1049.
suggested_fix: Add a global `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { *, *::before, *::after { animation-duration: 0.01ms !important; animation-iteration-count: 1 !important; } }` block to globals.css, and drop the pulse from the TV prize rows, which are being read rather than glanced at.
verify_note: Confirmed: the only prefers-reduced-motion match in src/ is the comment at display-ui.tsx:814 saying a static badge needs no opt-out, and there are 16 animate-pulse usages including the pre-call prize rows with staggered animationDelay (display-ui.tsx:986-993), the promo headline class (663), the player's Checking Claim card (728) and the host ON BREAK banner (1072), all indefinite with no pause control. Low is right: animate-pulse is an opacity fade rather than translation, which is the least provocative class of motion for vestibular sensitivity, and the WCAG 2.2.2 exposure is real but modest.

title: The pub TV's only outage signal is 14px white-on-amber with a 24px Refresh button
summary: When a live game is on screen the display never falls back to the large 'failed' panel (a renderable game deliberately outranks it), so a stalled TV shows the last ball plus a small amber pill nobody in the room can read.
failure_scenario: Realtime and polling both stall while a game is renderable. The TV keeps showing ball 43 as though it were current. The only cue is a `text-sm` pill at the top with roughly 1.8:1 contrast, unreadable at 10 metres, and its "Refresh" control is about 24x20px on a screen with no pointer. Punters keep marking a board that has stopped advancing until the 30s auto-reload fires (see the offline-reload finding).
evidence: connection-banner.tsx:23 `className="fixed top-2 left-1/2 -translate-x-1/2 z-50 flex items-center gap-3 rounded-full bg-amber-500/90 px-4 py-2 text-sm text-white shadow"` and lines 27-33 `className="ml-2 rounded bg-white/20 px-2 py-1 text-xs"`. White on amber-500 is ~1.8:1. display-ui.tsx:600-606 documents that `hasRenderableGame` beats `connectionPhase === 'failed'`, so the large legible panel at lines 766-786 never appears in this case. The banner is also z-50 while the win overlay is z-[80], so a stall during a win celebration hides it completely.
suggested_fix: Give ConnectionBanner a size variant: on /display render it at the same clamp() scale as the rest of the TV chrome, drop the Refresh button there (no pointer exists), and raise its z-index above the win overlay.
verify_note: The mechanics are as described: loadPhase in display-ui.tsx:599-605 puts 'active' ahead of 'failed' (documented deliberately at 592-598), so a renderable game keeps the large clamp() panel at 766-786 off screen and leaves only the fixed pill at connection-banner.tsx:23. White on amber-500 measures 2.15:1, the text is text-sm and the Refresh control is px-2 py-1 text-xs. z-50 is genuinely below the z-[70] validation overlay and z-[80] win overlay, and nothing in the root div creates a competing stacking context, so it is hidden during a win. Correcting severity down to low: the precedence rule is documented intentional design and the exposure is bounded, the banner appears at 10s and the auto-reload fires at 30s, so a stale board is on screen for at most 20s before the page reloads itself (assuming the network is up, which is the separate offline finding).

title: Host session rows expand via a bare div onClick with no keyboard or screen-reader affordance
summary: The only way to see a session's games on /host is to tap a plain div; it has no role, tabIndex, key handler or aria-expanded.
failure_scenario: A host using an external keyboard on a tablet, or any assistive technology, tabs through /host and reaches nothing: the session card is not focusable, so the games list cannot be opened and no game can be started. Screen-reader users get no announcement that the row is expandable or expanded.
evidence: Lines 89-92: `<div onClick={() => toggleSession(session.id)} className="p-4 flex items-center justify-between cursor-pointer">` with no role, tabIndex, onKeyDown or aria-expanded, and a purely decorative `▼` at line 109-111 as the only state signal.
suggested_fix: Make the row a `<button type="button">` with `aria-expanded={expandedSessionId === session.id}` and `aria-controls` pointing at the games panel.
verify_note: Verified: dashboard.tsx:88-92 is a plain div with onClick and cursor-pointer, no role, tabIndex, onKeyDown or aria-expanded, and the ▼ at 109-111 is the only state signal. It is a clear WCAG 2.1.1 (Level A) keyboard failure with no alternative route, since a game must be started from this list before its URL is usable. Correcting severity down to low on real-world impact: /host is a staff-only touch surface (phone or tablet) and every other affordance on it is tap-driven; there is no realistic pub scenario where the host is driving this screen from a keyboard or screen reader. Worth fixing as a two-line change, not a live-game risk.

title: Sign Out is a one-tap unconfirmed control in the top-right of the live host screen, next to a 32px back arrow
summary: The live game control page keeps a sticky header whose only right-hand control signs the host out mid-game with no confirmation, and whose back arrow is below the 44px target minimum.
failure_scenario: Host reaches for the top-right of the phone mid-game (the reflex spot for dismissing things) and hits Sign Out. The session cookie is cleared, they land on /login, the controller heartbeat stops and the game is left with a stale controlling_host_id for 30 seconds. They must re-enter credentials they may not know (staff accounts are invite-only and created out of band) before they can call the next number.
evidence:
Lines 104-108: `
` inside a `sticky top-0 z-20` header. Lines 91-95: the back link's Button is `className="h-8 px-2"` with `←` as its only content, giving roughly 32x28px.
suggested_fix: Remove Sign Out from the live game header entirely (it is available on /host), or gate it behind a confirm modal. Raise the back control to min-h-[44px] min-w-[44px] and give it an aria-label.
verify_note: Markup is as described: page.tsx:104-108 puts an unconfirmed Sign Out form in a sticky header on the live game page, and the back link's Button at 91-95 is h-8 px-2 (~32px). Correcting severity down to low. The stated consequence is wrong in one respect I checked: controlling_host_id holds the user's own id, so after signing back in the same account is still the controller (isController compares controlling_host_id to currentUserId) and calling resumes immediately, with no 30s lockout. The residual risk is a deliberate tap on a small, clearly labelled text button costing a re-login, and staff credentials are a login-screen problem, not a controller-lock one.

title: Resetting or deleting a snowball pot -- the app's most money-sensitive admin actions -- is guarded only by window.confirm
summary: Deleting a session or a game requires typing the exact name, but wiping an accumulated jackpot back to its base value needs one tap on a native OK, from a 32px ghost button in a table row.
failure_scenario: Admin means to tap "Edit" on the Friday pot but lands on "Reset" (both are `h-8 px-2` ghost buttons, 8px apart). The native confirm appears, they tap OK by reflex on a phone, and a pot that had rolled over to £340 across six weeks is reset to £200. The pot value is not versioned in snowball_pot_history for a manual reset the way a settlement is, so the number has to be reconstructed by hand.
evidence: Line 74 `if (confirm('Reset this pot to its BASE values? This clears the current jackpot.'))`; line 62 `if (confirm('Delete this snowball pot? This will unlink any games using it.'))`. Both buttons at lines 133-136 are `size="sm" ... h-8 px-2` in a `space-x-2` row. Compare admin/dashboard.tsx:119 `const isDeleteConfirmed = deleteTarget !== null && deleteTyped === deleteTarget.name;` and session-detail.tsx:270-273, which both require a typed confirmation for less costly operations.
suggested_fix: Use the same typed-confirm Modal pattern for pot reset and pot delete, and show the current value in the dialog ("This will clear £340 back to £200").
verify_note: The guard claim is true: snowball-list.tsx:62 and :74 use window.confirm only, and Reset / Edit / Delete are three h-8 px-2 ghost buttons in a space-x-2 row, while admin/dashboard.tsx:119 and session-detail.tsx:270-273 demand a typed name for less costly deletes. But the stated harm is refuted, which is why I am dropping the severity: resetSnowballPot (admin/snowball/actions.ts:187-250) refuses outright while any linked game is in_progress, reads the pot first, and inserts a snowball_pot_history row with change_type 'manual_reset' carrying old_val_max, new_val_max, old_val_jackpot, new_val_jackpot and changed_by. A wrongly reset £340 pot is recoverable from that audit row in one edit, not 'reconstructed by hand', and it cannot happen mid-game.

title: Closing a stacked modal restores page scrolling while the modal underneath is still open
summary: Modal sets document.body.style.overflow on open and unconditionally resets it to 'unset' on cleanup, so the Record Winner modal closing releases the scroll lock that the Validation modal underneath still needs.
failure_scenario: Host confirms a winner. Record Winner closes, its cleanup sets body overflow to 'unset', and the Post Win modal opens. The page behind both modals is now scrollable, so a scroll gesture aimed at the modal content moves the page underneath instead, and the modal appears to drift on the screen.
evidence: Lines 78-85: `useEffect(() => { if (isOpen) { document.body.style.overflow = "hidden"; } return () => { document.body.style.overflow = "unset"; }; }, [isOpen]);` -- the cleanup does not check whether another Modal instance is still mounted and open.
suggested_fix: Track open modals in a module-level counter and only restore overflow when the count reaches zero.
verify_note: The headline holds but the quoted scenario does not, so treat the failure text as corrected. modal.tsx:78-85 does reset body overflow to 'unset' unconditionally. However React runs all effect destroy functions before any create functions in a commit, and handleRecordWinner batches setShowWinnerModal(false), clearSpentClaim() and setShowPostWinModal(true) into one update, so the Post Win modal's effect re-applies overflow:hidden after the Record Winner cleanup and the page is NOT left scrollable on that path. The reachable path is handleCloseRecordWinnerModal (line 900), which closes Record Winner while the validation modal underneath stays open and unchanged, so its effect never re-runs and the body is left 'unset'. Consequence is scroll-chaining behind a fixed full-viewport overlay. Low is right.

title: The pub TV never shows the full called-numbers board; at 88 calls only the newest ~11 balls are visible
summary: The footer strip renders every called number in a single non-scrolling flex row with overflow-hidden and a fade mask, so all but the last handful are silently hidden, and there is no other view of the board on the big screen.
failure_scenario: At 88 calls a punter looks up to check whether 12 has gone. The strip shows roughly the last eleven balls, masked at the right edge with no cue that 77 more are hidden. "Total Calls: 88" is the only hint. Their only recourse is to scan the QR, open the phone follower and tap "View All Numbers" -- a control which, on a pale game colour, is itself invisible (see the background-colour finding).
evidence: Lines 1075-1084: `<div className="flex items-center gap-3 overflow-hidden mask-linear-fade">` mapping `delayedNumbers.slice().reverse()` with fixed 5.6rem / 4.2rem balls. At 1920px the right-hand footer cell is ~896px wide, fitting about eleven balls (89.6 + n x 79.2 <= 896). No other component on /display renders a 1-90 board.
suggested_fix: Add a compact 90-cell called board to the TV -- either in place of the empty left footer cell during a game, or as a periodic alternate view during long gaps between calls.
verify_note: Confirmed: display-ui.tsx:1073-1084 renders delayedNumbers reversed into a single flex row with overflow-hidden and .mask-linear-fade (globals.css:232-236 fades the last 3.5rem), balls fixed at 5.6rem/4.2rem with shrink-0, no scroll and no wrap, and no other component on /display renders a 1-90 grid. So at 88 calls the strip shows roughly the newest dozen with only 'Total Calls' as a hint. Low is right: this reads as a deliberate layout choice for the big screen (the full board lives on the player follower), not a broken code path.

title: The TV's "Connecting to game…" state is default 16px text, unlike every other display state
summary: The loading phase renders unscaled body text centred on the big screen, while the adjacent 'failed' state correctly uses clamp() typography sized for the room.
failure_scenario: The TV is switched on before the session data is available. The whole 55" screen is plain dark green with a line of 16px text in the middle, which reads as a broken or blank screen from the floor. Ten seconds later the same outage, once classified as 'failed', renders a 4rem headline.
evidence: Lines 755-762: `<div className="flex h-screen items-center justify-center text-white" ...>` with a bare `Connecting to game…` string and no font-size class, against lines 774-783 which use `text-[clamp(2rem,4.6vw,4.2rem)]` and `text-[clamp(1rem,1.55vw,1.35rem)]`.
suggested_fix: Reuse the 'failed' screen's typography (and its role="status" aria-live) for the loading phase.
verify_note: Confirmed: display-ui.tsx:755-762 renders a bare 'Connecting to game…' string with no font-size class, against the clamp(2rem,4.6vw,4.2rem) headline in the adjacent failed branch at 774-783. Low is right, and if anything generous: the comment at 752-754 notes the loading phase is deliberately brief because the first poll response resolves it to waiting, active, completed or failed, so the small text is on screen for a second or two, not for the ten seconds the scenario implies.

title: The "View Only Mode" overlay covers the current ball on a second device, and offers no way forward when the other host's tab is still alive
summary: The controller-lock banner is absolutely positioned over the top of the main display card, hiding the nickname and the top of the current number, and when canTakeControl is false it shows no owner, no timer and no route to recover.
failure_scenario: A host runs the game from a tablet and opens the same page on their phone to watch the count. The phone shows the View Only banner floating over the main card, obscuring the nickname and part of the giant ball, so the second screen cannot do the one thing it was opened for. Separately, a colleague leaves the host page open on the back-office PC and goes home: their heartbeat keeps firing every 10s, canTakeControl stays false forever, and the host on the floor sees only "Another host is currently controlling this game" with no Take Control button, no name, and no explanation of what to do.
evidence: Lines 1039-1058: `<div className="absolute inset-x-0 top-0 z-50 p-4">` inside the page container `<div className="p-4 pb-24 max-w-5xl mx-auto relative ...">`, so it paints over the first ~100px of the main Card at line 1076. canTakeControl (lines 149-150) is `!controlling_host_id || (controller_last_seen_at && now - last_seen > 30000)`; the branch at line 1046 renders the Take Control button only when that is true, and the else branch renders nothing extra.
suggested_fix: Make the banner a normal in-flow block above the card rather than an absolute overlay, and when canTakeControl is false show how long ago the controller was last seen plus the plain-English instruction ("the other device must close the game page, or wait 30 seconds after it goes offline").
verify_note: Geometry checks out: the banner at game-control.tsx:1039 is absolute inset-x-0 top-0 inside the relative page container, so its own p-4 puts it exactly where the first flow child starts. The ConnectionBanner is fixed and the alert rows are conditional, so with no alert showing it paints over the top of the main Card at line 1076, covering the nickname and the top of the 128px ball. canTakeControl (lines 148-150) is as quoted and the else branch adds nothing. Correcting severity down to low: this only ever affects a passive second screen (the whole control pad is already opacity-50 pointer-events-none in this state), and the 'locked out forever' half is the controller lock working as designed. A background tab gets its 10s heartbeat throttled to roughly once a minute, which exceeds the 30s window and hands control over anyway; only a foregrounded, awake second tab holds the lock, and closing it resolves it in 30s. The genuine gap is the missing explanation and countdown, which is copy.
